dive.topic: IP Helper API (GetIpInterfaceEntry/SetIpInterfaceEntry/MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW) via windows-rs, for interface-metric steering in LinkSwitch
dive.summary:
Verified against learn.microsoft.com AND by actually compiling/running code with windows-rs 0.62.2 (rustc 1.96.1) on this Windows 11 x86_64 machine, unelevated.

Core API: MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW is keyed by (Family, InterfaceLuid|InterfaceIndex). Before Get: zero the struct (MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW::default() or InitializeIpInterfaceEntry), set Family = AF_INET or AF_INET6, set InterfaceIndex (or InterfaceLuid). Call GetIpInterfaceEntry to fill the rest, mutate Metric/UseAutomaticMetric, then call SetIpInterfaceEntry with the SAME row. THE TRAP (confirmed twice in MS docs, verbatim): for AF_INET, SitePrefixLength must be forced back to 0 immediately before SetIpInterfaceEntry — Get populates it with a real value (64 was observed on this machine's loopback adapter) and passing that value straight through to Set fails with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87). This reset is NOT applicable/needed for AF_INET6 (round-trip that field unchanged for v6). Metric semantics: UseAutomaticMetric=true means Metric is stack-computed and ignored on Set; set UseAutomaticMetric=false and Metric=N for a manual metric; set UseAutomaticMetric=true to restore automatic (Metric value then irrelevant) — one SetIpInterfaceEntry call each way, no separate "clear" API. Do this once per address family (AF_INET and AF_INET6 are independent MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW rows on the same InterfaceIndex — steering one family leaves the other's default route untouched, so LinkSwitch must set both).

Privileges (empirically reproduced unelevated on this machine): GetIpInterfaceEntry and GetIpInterfaceTable need NO privilege — both succeeded unelevated, enumerating real adapters (12 rows across AF_INET/AF_INET6). SetIpInterfaceEntry returned WIN32_ERROR(5)=ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED unelevated regardless of SitePrefixLength handling, confirming MS docs: caller must hold an elevated Administrator token (built-in Administrator, OR an app manifested requestedExecutionLevel=requireAdministrator, OR an elevated shell) — Administrators-group membership alone, unelevated, still fails. This directly justifies LinkSwitch's Task-Scheduler-HIGHEST-run-level design.

Cargo/features (nailed down by actually building against the real crate source, not guessing from naming convention): enabling only "Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper" FAILS — cargo's own compile error points at `#[cfg(all(feature = "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis", feature = "Win32_Networking_WinSock"))]` gating GetIpInterfaceEntry, SetIpInterfaceEntry, InitializeIpInterfaceEntry, GetIpInterfaceTable and the MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW/MIB_IPINTERFACE_TABLE structs. Root cause (found by grepping vendored source): MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW.InterfaceLuid is NET_LUID_LH which lives in Win32::NetworkManagement::Ndis, while Family (ADDRESS_FAMILY) and three enum fields (RouterDiscoveryBehavior, LinkLocalAddressBehavior, TransmitOffload/ReceiveOffload's NL_INTERFACE_OFFLOAD_ROD) live in Win32::Networking::WinSock — BOTH extra features are mandatory. Win32_Foundation is NOT needed explicitly: IpHelper implies NetworkManagement implies Win32 implies Win32_Foundation transitively (verified: clean build with only 3 features, code references windows::Win32::Foundation::WIN32_ERROR directly with zero errors). FreeMibTable needs only Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper (untyped `*const c_void` param, no extra cfg gate). windows crate version confirmed: 0.62.2 (rust-version 1.82, edition 2021).

netsh (live `/?` output captured on this exact Windows 11 build): `netsh interface ipv4 set interface` and `netsh interface ipv6 set interface` share IDENTICAL syntax on this build, support `metric=<integer>`, but show NO documented "automatic" keyword — netsh is a one-way manual-metric tool; PowerShell's Set-NetIPInterface -AutomaticMetric Enabled is the documented way to restore automatic.

code.purpose: Core get/set-metric routine for ONE address family, with the SitePrefixLength=0 trap handled for IPv4 only. Empirically compiled and run against real adapters on this machine (unelevated Get succeeded; unelevated Set correctly returned ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED).

Enumerate all interfaces/families with GetIpInterfaceTable, correctly walking the ANYSIZE_ARRAY-style Table field via raw pointer arithmetic (NOT slice indexing), then freeing with FreeMibTable. Compiled and run on this machine: printed 12 real rows (AF_INET + AF_INET6 interleaved) unelevated.
Documented, working fallback/cross-check for both directions (manual metric and restoring automatic). Confirmed against the live Set-NetIPInterface reference.
code.snippet:
# Force Ethernet to lose the route race (raise its metric), on both v4 and v6:
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" -AddressFamily IPv4 -InterfaceMetric 9999
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" -AddressFamily IPv6 -InterfaceMetric 9999

# Restore automatic metric on both families (the "back to normal" / --apply auto path):
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" -AddressFamily IPv4  -AutomaticMetric Enabled
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" -AddressFamily IPv6  -AutomaticMetric Enabled

# Cross-check what actually landed:
Get-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet" |
    Select-Object InterfaceAlias, AddressFamily, InterfaceMetric, AutomaticMetric

code.purpose: netsh equivalent (manual metric only — no documented "automatic" keyword on this build, verified via live /? output), by interface name or index
code.snippet:
netsh interface ipv4 set interface "Ethernet" metric=9999
netsh interface ipv6 set interface "Ethernet" metric=9999

# by index instead of name (index is accepted per the live help text):
netsh interface ipv4 set interface interface=12 metric=9999

gotchas: The SitePrefixLength=0 reset must happen on EVERY SetIpInterfaceEntry call for an AF_INET row, not just metric changes — it's a property of the (Family=AF_INET, Set) combination, unconditional on what else is being changed. Forgetting it after a fresh Get is the single most common way to hit ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87) with this API; do it unconditionally in a shared helper rather than remembering it ad hoc at each call site.

"Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper" alone is not enough to compile ANY of GetIpInterfaceEntry/SetIpInterfaceEntry/GetIpInterfaceTable/MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW — you also need "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis" AND "Win32_Networking_WinSock". This is easy to miss because the feature name doesn't hint at the dependency, and docs.rs itself 404s on these pages (the windows crate is NOT built with all-features on docs.rs; use https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/ instead, which is the crate's own `documentation =` URL in Cargo.toml).

MIB_IPINTERFACE_TABLE.Table in windows-rs is a fixed `[MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW; 1]`, not a Vec or slice — indexing it normally (`table.Table[i]`) beyond i=0 is a runtime bounds-check panic. Must use `.Table.as_ptr().add(i)` and dereference.
MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW has no Debug/PartialEq derive in this crate version — `{:?}` won't work on it; write your own field-by-field logger if you need one for diagnostics/logging in the elevated worker.

Being a member of the local Administrators group is NOT sufficient for SetIpInterfaceEntry if the process token isn't elevated — this is exactly the UAC split-token problem the Task-Scheduler-HIGHEST-run-level design in the project brief is built to route around. Don't assume IsUserAnAdmin()/group-membership checks are a valid substitute for actually attempting the call / checking the real token elevation state.

AF_INET and AF_INET6 are two fully separate MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW entries for the same InterfaceIndex. A --apply that only touches one family will leave the other family's default-route selection unaffected — for a widget promising "all traffic" switches to Wi-Fi, both must be set together (see steer_interface above).

InterfaceIndex "may change when a network adapter is disabled and then enabled... and should not be considered persistent" per MS docs — for a config file that survives reboots/driver reinstalls, persist InterfaceLuid (or a friendly name resolved at run time via ConvertInterfaceIndexToLuid/GetIpInterfaceTable) rather than a raw InterfaceIndex.

docs.rs pages for this crate/version 404 for anything beyond the default-feature surface (confirmed: docs.rs/windows/0.62.2/.../fn.GetIpInterfaceEntry.html returns "This page does not exist" even though the crate version itself resolves) — always cross-check with the mirror at microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/... which IS built with all features, or grep the vendored source directly under %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\registry\src\...\windows-<version>\src\Windows\...
open_questions: Whether ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87) is actually returned (as opposed to ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED masking it first) when an ELEVATED process forgets the SitePrefixLength=0 reset on AF_INET — could not be isolated in this research session since only an unelevated shell was available; the MS documentation states the requirement unconditionally (independent of privilege) so the implementer should keep the reset regardless, but empirical confirmation of the exact error-precedence order under elevation is still open. Recommend a quick elevated smoke test during implementation (e.g. via the project's own --install-tasks/--apply plumbing) before relying on error-code branching for user-facing messages.

Whether InitializeIpInterfaceEntry followed by manually setting Family+InterfaceIndex is meaningfully different in practice from MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW::default() (also a zero-fill) followed by the same — MS docs recommend InitializeIpInterfaceEntry as "the" way to get default values, but the windows-rs Default impl is a plain zeroed() and this research did not turn up any field where zero-fill and InitializeIpInterfaceEntry's fill would actually differ. Treat MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW::default() as sufficient today but keep an eye on this if Microsoft ever changes InitializeIpInterfaceEntry's behavior.

Exact behavior of `netsh ... metric=0` was not empirically tested (would require an elevated shell to observe a real state change rather than an access-denied no-op) — some community reports claim metric=0 restores automatic via netsh, but this is undocumented in the live help text on this build and should not be relied on for LinkSwitch's netsh-fallback path; prefer PowerShell's explicitly-documented -AutomaticMetric Enabled for that direction.

verification.topic: IP Helper API (GetIpInterfaceEntry/SetIpInterfaceEntry/MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW) via windows-rs, for interface-metric steering in LinkSwitch

refuted.claim: The `explain()` helper in the research's Rust snippet maps errors back to WIN32_ERROR via `WIN32_ERROR(e.code().0 as u32)` and compares against ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED / ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND / ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER
refuted.why_wrong: BROKEN — every branch is dead code. `WIN32_ERROR::ok()` in windows-0.62.2 does `Err(self.to_hresult().into())`, i.e. `HRESULT::from_win32(5)` = 0x80070005, NOT 5. So `e.code().0 as u32` == 2147942405 and `WIN32_ERROR(2147942405) == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (WIN32_ERROR(5))` is FALSE. Proved empirically (built + ran): 'hresult = 0x80070005 / comparison == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED ? false / explain() would say: other'. Source: %USERPROFILE%\.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f\windows-0.62.2\src\extensions\Win32\Foundation\WIN32_ERROR.rs lines 12-31. Consequence: LinkSwitch's user-facing message would always be the fallback and would never say 'not elevated'.
refuted.correction: Two correct options, both compiled and run here. (a) BEST: never convert to windows::core::Error at all — GetIpInterfaceEntry/SetIpInterfaceEntry already return WIN32_ERROR, so drop the `.ok()?` and match on the raw code: `let rc = unsafe { SetIpInterfaceEntry(&mut row) }; if rc.is_err() { ... }` then `match rc { NO_ERROR => .., ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED => .., ERROR_NOT_FOUND => .., ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND => .., ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER => .., _ => .. }` (WIN32_ERROR consts are usable as match patterns — verified). (b) If you already hold a `windows::core::Error`, the crate ships the exact un-mangler: `windows::Win32::Foundation::WIN32_ERROR::from_error(&e) -> Option<WIN32_ERROR>` — returns `Some(WIN32_ERROR(5))` (verified). Equivalent: `e.code() == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED.to_hresult()` (verified true).

refuted.claim: `steer_interface(if_index, metric)` should set AF_INET then AF_INET6 with `?` propagation, because 'AF_INET and AF_INET6 are independent rows on the same InterfaceIndex' and 'both must be set together'
refuted.why_wrong: REFUTED ON REAL HARDWARE. Most adapters do not have an IPv6 row at all, and the v6 leg returns ERROR_NOT_FOUND (1168), which `?` turns into a hard failure that ALSO discards the successful IPv4 change's result. Measured read-only on this Windows 11 box (10 IPv4 rows but only 2 IPv6 rows out of 12 total): GetIpInterfaceEntry(AF_INET6) rc=1168 for ifIndex 4, 6, 14, 16, 17, 19, 23, 43; rc=0 only for 1 (loopback) and 39 (Hyper-V vSwitch). The physical NICs here have IPv6 unbound. The research's own enumeration output ('12 rows') contained this evidence and it was not noticed. Worse, the research's error taxonomy never mentions ERROR_NOT_FOUND (1168) at all — `explain()` lists ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (2) instead, and those are DIFFERENT cases per learn.microsoft.com: 2 = the LUID/index is not on the machine; 1168 = the interface exists but does not match the requested address family. Verified separately: Get on a bogus index 999999 returns 2, Get on a real index with an unbound family returns 1168.

refuted.claim: open_question #2: 'this research did not turn up any field where zero-fill and InitializeIpInterfaceEntry's fill would actually differ. Treat MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW::default() as sufficient today'
refuted.why_wrong: REFUTED, and the truth is a Rust UNDEFINED-BEHAVIOUR hazard, not a cosmetic difference. Ran a byte-for-byte comparison: sizeof(MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW)=168, and 132 of 168 bytes differ between `default()` (all zero) and post-`InitializeIpInterfaceEntry`. Initialize fills with 0xFF 'leave unchanged' sentinels: SitePrefixLength=0xFFFFFFFF, Metric=0xFFFFFFFF, MaxReassemblySize=0xFFFFFFFF, DadTransmits=0xFFFFFFFF, RouterDiscoveryBehavior=-1 (RouterDiscoveryUnchanged), LinkLocalAddressBehavior=-1 (LinkLocalUnchanged). Critically, windows-rs models the C `BOOLEAN` (unsigned char) members as Rust `bool`, and Initialize writes raw 0xFF into them — measured raw bytes: offset 40 (AdvertisingEnabled)=0xFF, offset 44 (UseAutomaticMetric)=0xFF, offset 156 (Connected)=0xFF. A Rust `bool` holding 0xFF is an invalid bit pattern; merely reading `row.UseAutomaticMetric` after InitializeIpInterfaceEntry is instant UB (it happens to print 'true' today under debug codegen, which is exactly how this stays hidden).
refuted.correction: Do NOT call InitializeIpInterfaceEntry from Rust. The safe, documented-equivalent pattern is exactly what the research's main snippet already does: `MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW::default()` (a real zeroing `impl Default` in windows-0.62.2, IpHelper/mod.rs:3005-3009) -> set Family + InterfaceIndex -> `GetIpInterfaceEntry` -> mutate -> `SetIpInterfaceEntry`. Get overwrites every field with stack-supplied 0/1 booleans, so no invalid bool ever exists. Note also that the SitePrefixLength=0 reset is MORE necessary on the Initialize path (it leaves 0xFFFFFFFF there), which is why learn.microsoft.com repeats the warning in both Remarks paragraphs.

refuted.claim: Claim 4 cites the SitePrefixLength=0 requirement to BOTH nf-netioapi-setipinterfaceentry AND ns-netioapi-mib_ipinterface_row ('SitePrefixLength member doc')
refuted.why_wrong: Half the citation is fabricated. I fetched ns-netioapi-mib_ipinterface_row in full: its SitePrefixLength member text is only 'The site prefix length, in bits, of the IP interface address... For an IPv4 address, any value greater than 32 is an illegal value. For an IPv6 address, any value greater than 128 is an illegal value. A value of 255 is commonly used to represent an illegal value.' There is NO mention of a must-be-0-on-Set rule anywhere on that page. The rule appears ONLY on the SetIpInterfaceEntry page (and there it is genuinely stated twice, verbatim: 'However for IPv4, an application must not try to modify the SitePrefixLength member of the MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW structure. For IPv4, the SitePrefixLength member must be set to 0.').
refuted.correction: Keep the SitePrefixLength=0 behaviour (the requirement IS real and IS stated twice), but cite only https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/netioapi/nf-netioapi-setipinterfaceentry. The struct page independently explains WHY it fails: Get returns 64 for AF_INET, and 'any value greater than 32 is an illegal value' for IPv4.

refuted.claim: Claim 5: 'GetIpInterfaceEntry returned SitePrefixLength=64' on 'this machine's loopback adapter' (AF_INET)
refuted.why_wrong: Understated and it hid a pattern that matters. Re-measured read-only: SitePrefixLength=64 on EVERY auto-metric row, IPv4 AND IPv6 — ifIndex 1,4,6,14,16,17,19,23 all v4_spl=64, and loopback's v6 row is also 64. It is 0 only on the two rows that already carry a manual metric (ifIndex 39 and 43, UseAutomaticMetric=false). So this is not a loopback quirk — it is the value you will get back for the real Ethernet and Wi-Fi adapters LinkSwitch targets, on both families.
refuted.correction: Data table (read-only, this Windows 11 box): idx=1 v4_spl=64 v6_spl=64; idx=4/6/14/16/17/19/23 v4_spl=64, v6 rc=1168; idx=39 v4_spl=0 v6_spl=0 (manual metric 5000); idx=43 v4_spl=0 (manual metric 0), v6 rc=1168. Also note the research says to 'round-trip that field unchanged for v6' — that means writing 64 back on an IPv6 Set, which is untested by anyone (nobody in this research chain has ever run an elevated Set). It is legal per docs (<=128), but flag it as untested rather than as a verified recommendation.

refuted.claim: Claim 9: 'netsh interface ipv4/ipv6 set interface ... support metric=<integer>' as shown by the live /? output
refuted.why_wrong: The live /? output on this exact build does NOT list `metric=` in the Usage syntax line at all — I captured it: the usage shows [interface=] [forwarding=] [advertise=] [mtu=] [siteprefixlength=] [nud=] [basereachabletime=] [retransmittime=] [dadtransmits=] [routerdiscovery=] [managedaddress=] [otherstateful=] [weakhostsend=] [weakhostreceive=] [ignoredefaultroutes=] [advertisedrouterlifetime=] [advertisedefaultroute=] [currenthoplimit=] [store=] [forcearpndwolpattern=] [enabledirectedmacwolpattern=] [ecncapability=] [rabaseddnsconfig=] [dhcpstaticipcoexistence=]. `metric` appears ONLY down in the Parameters descriptions ('metric - Interface metric, added to route metrics for all routes over the interface'), an inconsistency in Microsoft's own help text. metric= does still work, but the research's framing ('the live /? output supports metric=') misreads its own capture. Separately, the research entirely missed `store=active|persistent` in that same output ('active: Set only lasts until next boot. persistent: Set is persistent.'), which is the single most decision-relevant flag for LinkSwitch.
refuted.correction: netsh: metric= is undocumented-in-usage but functional; ALWAYS pass `store=` explicitly since the default is not shown — `netsh interface ipv4 set interface "Ethernet" metric=9999 store=persistent` (survives reboot) vs `store=active` (reverts at boot — arguably the safer default for a toggle widget). The ipv4 and ipv6 grammars are byte-identical on this build, that part of claim 9 is confirmed.

added_gotchas: PERSISTENCE IS UNANSWERED AND IS LOAD-BEARING. netsh exposes store=active|persistent and Set-NetIPInterface exposes -PolicyStore ActiveStore|PersistentStore (MS docs, verbatim: 'If you do not specify this parameter, the default entries are created in both the ActiveStore and the PersistentStore'). SetIpInterfaceEntry has NO store parameter and learn.microsoft.com says nothing about reboot persistence. So the research's three mechanisms are NOT interchangeable: the PowerShell fallback it recommends writes BOTH stores by default (survives reboot), while the reboot behaviour of the IP Helper call it recommends as primary is undocumented. LinkSwitch must decide and then verify with an actual reboot: is a 'Wi-Fi mode' toggle supposed to survive a restart, or revert? Do not ship until measured.

windows-rs models C `BOOLEAN` (unsigned char) as Rust `bool` in MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW (UseAutomaticMetric, Connected, DisableDefaultRoutes, ...). Any Win32 path that leaves a non-0/1 byte in one of those makes reading it UB. Confirmed for InitializeIpInterfaceEntry (0xFF fill). Corollary: never memcpy/transmute a row from another source, never construct one by hand except via `::default()` + Get, and don't stash rows in a cache across calls.

MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW is `#[derive(Clone, Copy)]` with a hand-written `impl Default` and NO Debug/PartialEq — but note the row is 168 bytes and `Copy`, so `let mut row = original;` silently duplicates it. If you Get once and Set twice (v4 then v6) off the same variable you will send a stale Family. Build a fresh `::default()` per (index, family) pair, as the corrected helper does.

Get with `Family = AF_UNSPEC` returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87) — verified. AF_UNSPEC is legal ONLY for GetIpInterfaceTable, never for the single-entry Get/Set. The research's snippets happen to get this right but never state it, and it is an easy refactor trap when you unify the table and entry code paths.

`Set-NetIPInterface` with NO targeting parameter modifies EVERY interface on the box — MS docs, verbatim: 'If you do not specify any parameters, this cmdlet sets all of the IP interface properties on the computer, including virtual interfaces and loopback interfaces.' If LinkSwitch ever shells out to it with an empty/failed alias variable, it nukes the whole machine's metrics. Always pass -InterfaceIndex (numeric, validated) and -AddressFamily, and prefer -InterfaceIndex over -InterfaceAlias (aliases are user-renamable and localized).

ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (2) and ERROR_NOT_FOUND (1168) are BOTH reachable and mean different things — 2 = that LUID/index does not exist on this machine (adapter removed); 1168 = it exists but the address family is not bound to it (IPv6 unchecked in adapter properties). LinkSwitch's UI must distinguish them: 2 means 'reconfigure, your saved adapter is gone', 1168 on the v6 leg means 'fine, nothing to do'. Verified both empirically.

Restoring automatic metric cannot be done by remembering the old number. When UseAutomaticMetric=true, Get reports the STACK-COMPUTED value (observed here: 5 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 65 / 75 depending on link speed). Writing that number back would pin it as a manual metric that no longer tracks link-speed changes. Only `UseAutomaticMetric = true` restores automatic — the research states this correctly and it is worth keeping prominent. Also zero `Metric` when doing so (defensive; the docs do not say Set ignores Metric when UseAutomaticMetric is TRUE — the ignored-on-Set list on the SetIpInterfaceEntry page is MaxReassemblySize, Min/MaxRouterAdvertisementInterval, Connected, SupportsWakeUpPatterns, SupportsNeighborDiscovery, SupportsRouterDiscovery, ReachableTime, TransmitOffload, ReceiveOffload — Metric and UseAutomaticMetric are NOT on it).

GetIpInterfaceTable(AF_UNSPEC) here returned rows grouped by family (all 10 IPv4 rows, then the 2 IPv6 rows), not 'interleaved' as the research described. Do not rely on any ordering; key on (InterfaceIndex, Family).

The corrected minimal Cargo.toml is confirmed by build: `windows = { version = "0.62.2", features = ["Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper", "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis", "Win32_Networking_WinSock"] }` — a clean `cargo build` succeeded with those three while also naming `windows::Win32::Foundation::WIN32_ERROR`. The negative test is also confirmed: with ONLY Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper you get `error[E0432]: unresolved imports ... note: found an item that was configured out --> ...\IpHelper\mod.rs:487:15` and `:2967:12`. Adding "Win32_Foundation" explicitly is harmless and self-documenting.
verification.verdict: Mostly trustworthy on facts, NOT safe to build on as code. The factual spine holds up under independent checking: windows 0.62.2 really is the newest crates.io version (published 2025-10-06); the three-feature requirement is exactly right and I reproduced both the passing build and the E0432 "configured out" failure; the SitePrefixLength=0-for-IPv4 rule is genuinely stated twice on the SetIpInterfaceEntry page; the elevation requirement is real and quoted correctly; the ANYSIZE_ARRAY `[MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW; 1]` walk, the missing Debug/PartialEq, ADDRESS_FAMILY(u16)/AF_INET=2/AF_INET6=23, NET_LUID_LH-as-opaque, the docs.rs 404 vs microsoft.github.io mirror, and the Set-NetIPInterface parameter surface all check out verbatim. But BOTH Rust snippets, which is what an implementer would actually paste, contain defects that compile cleanly and then misbehave: `explain()` compares a mangled HRESULT against a WIN32_ERROR so every branch is dead (proved: 0x80070005 != 5), and `steer_interface`'s `?` on the IPv6 leg fails on 8 of the 10 interfaces on this very machine because IPv6 is unbound (ERROR_NOT_FOUND 1168, a code the research never mentions). One open question is answered backwards — InitializeIpInterfaceEntry differs from zeroed() in 132 of 168 bytes and poisons Rust `bool` fields with 0xFF, which is UB, not a non-issue. And the one thing a reboot-surviving desktop widget most needs to know — whether SetIpInterfaceEntry writes the persistent store — is never raised, even though the netsh `store=` flag was sitting in the research's own captured output. Take the API facts and the Cargo.toml; rewrite the two functions using the corrected versions above (both compiled and run here).

dive.topic: Rust (windows-rs) adapter enumeration, live network-state reads, and default-route determination for LinkSwitch
dive.summary: All APIs verified against windows crate 0.62.2 (docs.rs stub redirects to the Microsoft-hosted full-feature mirror at microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs, which I used for exact signatures; feature names cross-checked against the real docs.rs/crate/windows/latest/features page). GetAdaptersAddresses lives in windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::IpHelper (feature Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper), returns raw u32 (not WIN32_ERROR), takes Option-wrapped nullable pointer params. IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH additionally needs Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis (for IF_OPER_STATUS/NET_LUID_LH) and Win32_Networking_WinSock (for SOCKET_ADDRESS/SOCKADDR). Microsoft's own official C sample prescribes a 15000-byte initial buffer, MAX_TRIES=3, retry only on ERROR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW — translated exactly to Rust with a Vec<u8> buffer. IN_ADDR/IN6_ADDR have direct From/Into impls with std::net::Ipv4Addr/Ipv6Addr (no manual byte-swapping needed). For discriminating real hardware NICs from virtual/loopback/tunnel/Bluetooth-PAN adapters, IfType filtering (Ethernet=6, IEEE80211=71) is necessary but not sufficient — the reliable additional signal, confirmed against Microsoft's netioapi MIB_IF_ROW2 docs and cross-validated against WireGuard-for-Windows' winipcfg Go package, is MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags.HardwareInterface (bit 0, mask 0x01), fetched per-adapter via GetIfEntry2(InterfaceLuid=adapter.Luid). This is a raw `_bitfield: u8` in windows-rs with no generated accessors — must mask manually. For "who wins the default route," GetBestRoute2 against a public destination is authoritative (it is the OS's actual route-selection code path, honoring the documented effective-metric rule: interface metric + route metric, longest-prefix-first) versus manually walking GetIpForwardTable2 and reimplementing that arithmetic, which is useful only for side-by-side diagnostic display. Live updates: NotifyIpInterfaceChange/NotifyRouteChange2/NotifyUnicastIpAddressChange each cover a different mutation (interface property change including our own metric writes; forwarding-table row add/delete; DHCP/address lease churn) so the widget needs all three registered, feeding a cloned Send+Sync egui::Context::request_repaint() from the OS notification thread. wlanapi (Win32_NetworkManagement_WiFi) is directly present in windows-rs with no dedicated crate needed or worth adding.

claims.claim: windows crate is currently at version 0.62.2 on crates.io; feature flag naming convention is Win32_<Category>_<Subcategory> matching the Rust module path exactly (e.g. windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::IpHelper ↔ feature "Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper")

docs.rs cannot successfully build full API docs for the windows crate (its own docs.rs page is a stub); the authoritative full-feature mirror is https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/, used here for all exact struct/fn signatures. It is built with every feature enabled so it never shows 'available on feature X' banners — feature requirements must be cross-checked against the real docs.rs features page instead.

GetAdaptersAddresses signature: pub unsafe fn GetAdaptersAddresses(family: u32, flags: GET_ADAPTERS_ADDRESSES_FLAGS, reserved: Option<*const c_void>, adapteraddresses: Option<*mut IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH>, sizepointer: *mut u32) -> u32. family is plain u32 (cast AF_UNSPEC.0 as u32); return is raw u32, not WIN32_ERROR.

Microsoft's own recommended buffer-sizing algorithm (official C sample) is: pre-allocate a 15,000-byte buffer, call once; only on ERROR_BUFFER_OVERFLOW free/reallocate to the size iphlpapi wrote back into SizePointer and retry, capped at MAX_TRIES=3 total attempts.

IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH requires Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper AND Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis AND Win32_Networking_WinSock enabled together (plus Win32_Foundation for HANDLE/error codes used elsewhere), consistent with the struct's field types (OperStatus: IF_OPER_STATUS lives in Ndis; unicast Address: SOCKET_ADDRESS lives in WinSock).
claims.source: web search of real-world Cargo.toml usage + https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/Win32/NetworkManagement/IpHelper/struct.IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH.html

claims.claim: IF_TYPE_ETHERNET_CSMACD=6 and IF_TYPE_IEEE80211=71 (and all other IF_TYPE_*/GAA_FLAG_* constants) live in windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::IpHelper, NOT in the Ndis module.

IF_OPER_STATUS (type + variants IfOperStatusUp/Down/Testing/Unknown/Dormant/NotPresent/LowerLayerDown) and NET_LUID_LH live in windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::Ndis (feature Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis), each generated as a #[repr(transparent)] struct(pub i32) newtype with free top-level constants, not a Rust enum.

MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags.HardwareInterface (bit 0, mask 0x01 of the packed BOOLEAN:1 bitfield, MSVC LSB-first packing) is Microsoft's own documented signal meaning 'this network interface is for hardware' — the best available first-party discriminator against virtual/software adapters (Hyper-V vEthernet, VMware, WSL, TAP/VPN, Bluetooth PAN). Cross-validated by WireGuard-for-Windows' own winipcfg Go bindings, which define IAOSFHardwareInterface = 1<<0 = 0x01.

In windows-rs, MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags has Rust type MIB_IF_ROW2_0, generated as a bare #[repr(C)] pub struct MIB_IF_ROW2_0 { pub _bitfield: u8 } with NO generated accessor methods — bits must be masked manually (bit0=HardwareInterface, bit1=FilterInterface, bit2=ConnectorPresent, bit3=NotAuthenticated, bit4=NotMediaConnected, bit5=Paused, bit6=LowPower, bit7=EndPointInterface).
GetIfEntry2(row: *mut MIB_IF_ROW2) -> WIN32_ERROR lives in the same IpHelper module/feature; populate row.InterfaceLuid (or InterfaceIndex) before calling.

GetBestRoute2 signature: pub unsafe fn GetBestRoute2(interfaceluid: Option<*const NET_LUID_LH>, interfaceindex: u32, sourceaddress: Option<*const SOCKADDR_INET>, destinationaddress: *const SOCKADDR_INET, addresssortoptions: u32, bestroute: *mut MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2, bestsourceaddress: *mut SOCKADDR_INET) -> WIN32_ERROR. Pass interfaceluid=None, interfaceindex=0, sourceaddress=None to let the OS pick using its real routing/policy logic.

GetIpForwardTable2(family: ADDRESS_FAMILY, table: *mut *mut MIB_IPFORWARD_TABLE2) -> WIN32_ERROR; rows are freed with FreeMibTable(memory: *const c_void). MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2 fields include InterfaceLuid, InterfaceIndex, DestinationPrefix (IP_ADDRESS_PREFIX { Prefix: SOCKADDR_INET, PrefixLength: u8 }), NextHop, Metric: u32, Protocol, Loopback/AutoconfigureAddress/Publish/Immortal: bool, Age, Origin. Default-route rows have DestinationPrefix.PrefixLength == 0.

Windows' documented route-selection rule (used internally by GetBestRoute2): longest matching prefix wins first; among equal-length-prefix matches, the route with the lowest EFFECTIVE metric wins, where effective metric = route's own Metric field + the owning interface's interface metric. Manually walking GetIpForwardTable2 for a 'who wins' answer requires re-implementing this addition+tie-break; GetBestRoute2 does it authoritatively and additionally accounts for policy/on-link rules GetIpForwardTable2 alone doesn't expose.

NotifyIpInterfaceChange(family: ADDRESS_FAMILY, callback: PIPINTERFACE_CHANGE_CALLBACK, callercontext: Option<*const c_void>, initialnotification: bool, notificationhandle: *mut HANDLE) -> WIN32_ERROR. Callback type: Option<unsafe extern "system" fn(callercontext: *const c_void, row: *const MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW, notificationtype: MIB_NOTIFICATION_TYPE)>. When initialnotification=true, the callback fires once immediately after registration with row=NULL and notificationtype=MibInitialNotification purely to confirm registration succeeded (not a real change).

Documented deadlock hazard: CancelMibChangeNotify2 must never be called from inside the notification callback itself (or from a thread holding a resource the callback thread waits on) — it must be called from a separate thread, or deadlock results. Also, when Row is non-null in the callback it contains only partial data; the callback should build a fresh MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW seeded with Family/InterfaceLuid/InterfaceIndex and call GetIpInterfaceEntry for full data, and must never free the Row pointer (OS-owned memory).

Changing an interface's own Metric (what LinkSwitch's --apply worker does via SetIpInterfaceEntry) is a MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW property mutation, so it fires NotifyIpInterfaceChange (MibParameterNotification) — it does NOT necessarily add/remove any 0.0.0.0/0 forwarding-table row, so NotifyRouteChange2 alone would likely miss the widget's own metric-steering action. All three Notify* APIs (interface, route table, unicast address) are needed together for complete 'why did my default path change' coverage.
claims.source: inference from documented MIB_NOTIFICATION_TYPE semantics (MibParameterNotification vs MibAddInstance/MibDeleteInstance) applied to what each table represents

claims.claim: egui::Context (current egui/eframe 0.36.1) is Clone + Send + Sync ('cheap to clone, clones refer to the same mutable data'), with methods request_repaint(&self), request_repaint_after(&self, duration: Duration), request_repaint_of(&self, id: ViewportId), and request_repaint_after_for. Safe to clone a Context into a static/global and call .request_repaint() directly from the IP Helper notification thread.

IN_ADDR and IN6_ADDR (windows::Win32::Networking::WinSock) each have direct impl From<IN_ADDR> for std::net::Ipv4Addr / impl From<Ipv4Addr> for IN_ADDR (and the IPv6 equivalents) — eliminates manual byte-order/union unpacking for converting a parsed SOCKADDR_IN/SOCKADDR_IN6 to a printable Rust IP address.

PWSTR (windows_core, used for FriendlyName/Description/DnsSuffix) exposes pub unsafe fn to_string(&self) -> Result<String, FromUtf16Error> and pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool (safe). Always null-check before calling to_string(); the pointer must be valid up to the next \0.

wlanapi is fully present in windows-rs under windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::WiFi (feature 'Win32_NetworkManagement_WiFi'), including WlanOpenHandle, WlanCloseHandle, WlanEnumInterfaces, WlanQueryInterface, WlanRegisterNotification, WlanFreeMemory, and structs WLAN_INTERFACE_INFO_LIST/WLAN_INTERFACE_INFO, WLAN_CONNECTION_ATTRIBUTES, WLAN_ASSOCIATION_ATTRIBUTES (dot11Ssid, wlanSignalQuality: u32 0-100, dot11Bssid, ulRxRate/ulTxRate), DOT11_SSID, and the opcode constant wlan_intf_opcode_current_connection: WLAN_INTF_OPCODE. No well-maintained third-party crate wraps this cleanly for Windows as of Sep 2026 — candidates found ('waifai', 'wifi-rs', 'wifi_scan') are Linux-focused (nmcli) or shell out to netsh rather than calling wlanapi directly, so calling windows-rs's own WiFi module directly is the right call; it is a self-contained ~5-function, ~100-150 line addition.

code.purpose: Buffer-resize loop + full adapter walk + SOCKADDR->IpAddr conversion (topic 1)
Reliable hardware-vs-virtual discriminator (topic 2) via GetIfEntry2 + HardwareInterface bit
Authoritative 'who wins the default route right now' via GetBestRoute2 (topic 3)
Notify* registration wired to egui repaint, with the deadlock/thread gotcha respected (topic 4)
wlanapi SSID + signal query for the currently connected Wi-Fi interface (topic 5)

gotchas: GetAdaptersAddresses returns raw u32, but most netioapi.h functions (GetBestRoute2, GetIpForwardTable2, Notify*, CancelMibChangeNotify2, GetIfEntry2) return WIN32_ERROR — don't assume a uniform return type across this API family; check each fn's exact signature.

GET_ADAPTERS_ADDRESSES_FLAGS, IF_OPER_STATUS, MIB_NOTIFICATION_TYPE, WLAN_INTF_OPCODE etc. are all #[repr(transparent)] struct(pub i32/u32) newtypes, NOT Rust enums — you cannot exhaustively match them and there's no compiler help catching a typo'd variant name; they're free top-level const items, easy to accidentally import from the wrong module.

IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH.Anonymous1 is a union covering the Length/IfIndex pair from the base structure's historical layout evolution — accessing it requires an extra unsafe union-field read; confirm the exact nested path (Anonymous1.Anonymous.IfIndex per the LH revision) against the live struct in the installed crate version before shipping, since anonymous nested-union field naming can shift subtly between windows-rs releases.
PWSTR::to_string()/as_wide() are unsafe fn — always call is_null() first; a null FriendlyName (rare but possible on some virtual adapters) would otherwise be UB if dereferenced.

CancelMibChangeNotify2 must never be invoked from inside the very callback it's canceling (or from a thread blocked on something the callback thread needs) — Microsoft explicitly documents this as a deadlock. Route the 'stop watching' action through a dedicated shutdown path, never directly inside on_*_change.

The MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW/MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2/MIB_UNICASTIPADDRESS_ROW pointers handed to the Notify* callbacks are OS-owned and only PARTIALLY populated (enough to re-query with GetIpInterfaceEntry/GetIfEntry2 by Luid) — never call FreeMibTable on them, and never treat their non-Luid/Family fields as authoritative.

Re-allocate the GetAdaptersAddresses buffer fresh on every retry iteration (vec![0u8; buf_len] each loop pass, as shown) mirroring the official C sample's malloc/free-per-iteration approach, rather than trying to reuse/resize the same Vec in place across the raw-pointer cast pattern.

Do not do real work (string formatting, GetAdaptersAddresses re-enumeration, egui layout) inside the extern "system" Notify* callback itself — it runs on an IP Helper-owned worker thread with undocumented stack/reentrancy constraints; only flip a flag / call request_repaint() there, and do the actual re-query on the next egui frame's update().

WLAN_INTERFACE_INFO_LIST.InterfaceInfo is a C flexible array member; in windows-rs it typically shows up as a fixed placeholder array — you must index past it manually using dwNumberOfItems and pointer arithmetic (.as_ptr().add(i)), not treat it as a real fixed-size Rust array.
open_questions: Exact windows-rs field path for IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH's IfIndex (Anonymous1 union naming) should be confirmed by checking the generated struct directly in the target crate version (e.g. via cargo doc --open on the actual pinned version), since anonymous-union field naming can differ subtly across 0.6x windows-rs releases and this could not be pinned with 100% certainty from the doc mirror alone.

Whether to additionally special-case NET_IF_CONNECTION_TYPE (Dedicated=1 for real Ethernet vs Passive=2 for e.g. RAS/some virtual adapters) as a tertiary filter alongside HardwareInterface — worth empirically testing on the dev machine against actual Hyper-V/VMware/WSL adapters before locking the filter logic, since Microsoft's docs don't promise virtual adapters are consistently non-Dedicated.

Should WlanRegisterNotification (push-based Wi-Fi state/SSID-change callback) be wired in alongside the three Notify* IP-layer callbacks, so an SSID change/roam updates the widget without waiting for the next IP-layer event? Not fully explored here since the brief's topic 4 named only the three IP Helper Notify* functions, but the WiFi module's WLAN_NOTIFICATION_CALLBACK exists and could be added at moderate extra cost.

Confirm at implementation time whether SetIpInterfaceEntry writes (in the separate --apply worker process) reliably fire NotifyIpInterfaceChange in the unelevated widget process — cross-process notification delivery for netioapi Notify* APIs is system-wide per Microsoft's docs (OS-level, not per-handle-to-a-specific-object), but this should be smoke-tested against the actual --apply implementation once written, since that's the core 'live update without polling' guarantee the whole widget UX depends on.

verification.topic: Rust (windows-rs) adapter enumeration, live network-state reads, and default-route determination for LinkSwitch
verification.verdict: TRUSTWORTHY ON API SURFACE, DANGEROUS ON ONE DESIGN RECOMMENDATION. This dive is unusually accurate — I built a real crate against windows 0.62.2 on this machine and ALL FIVE code snippets compile verbatim (4 warnings, 0 errors), and every fully-qualified path, constant value, feature name and struct field checks out against the vendored generated source. Build on it. But do NOT build on two things: (a) `GetBestRoute2` as the "who wins" answer — on this very machine it returns the ProtonVPN tunnel, not Ethernet or Wi-Fi, so the widget's core readout would be wrong whenever any VPN is up; (b) the claim that `NET_LUID_LH` is a `repr(transparent)` i32 newtype — it is a union with no `PartialEq`, and comparing two LUIDs (exactly what you must do to map a route back to an adapter) is a hard compile error. Also, the dive's whole `--apply` mechanism is one undocumented trap away from failing: `GetIpInterfaceEntry` returns `SitePrefixLength=64` for IPv4 on this box, and Microsoft documents that IPv4 `SetIpInterfaceEntry` requires it be 0 — a naive read-modify-write returns ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. That trap is absent from the dive.

refuted.claim: Claim 7: 'IF_OPER_STATUS ... and NET_LUID_LH live in windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::Ndis, EACH generated as a #[repr(transparent)] struct(pub i32) newtype with free top-level constants, not a Rust enum.'
refuted.why_wrong: True for IF_OPER_STATUS, FALSE for NET_LUID_LH. In the actual vendored source (windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/NetworkManagement/Ndis/mod.rs:2477) NET_LUID_LH is `pub union NET_LUID_LH { pub Value: u64, pub Info: NET_LUID_LH_0 }` — a union over u64, not an i32 newtype, with no associated constants. Critically it derives NO PartialEq. I compiled `let _ = NET_LUID_LH::default() == NET_LUID_LH::default();` and got a hard error: `error[E0369]: binary operation `==` cannot be applied to type `NET_LUID_LH``. This is load-bearing: the ONLY way to map GetBestRoute2's winning route back to an enumerated adapter is by LUID, and the dive's own probe-shaped code never does that comparison so the error is latent.
refuted.correction:
NET_LUID_LH is a union; compare via the u64 payload inside unsafe:

  #[inline]
  fn luid_eq(a: NET_LUID_LH, b: NET_LUID_LH) -> bool { unsafe { a.Value == b.Value } }

Store `unsafe { a.Luid.Value }` (a plain u64) in your Adapter struct instead of the raw union — then it is Eq/Hash/Debug and usable as a HashMap key. Same applies to `MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2.InterfaceLuid` and `MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceLuid`. Verified working: `unsafe { r.InterfaceLuid.Value } == unsafe { a.luid.Value }` correctly matched route ifIndex 43 to adapter 'ProtonVPN'.

refuted.claim: Claim 13 + the bestroute.rs snippet: 'GetBestRoute2 against a public destination is authoritative (it is the OS's actual route-selection code path)... GetIpForwardTable2 + manual (row.Metric + interface_metric) comparison is fine for a side-by-side diagnostics table but is a re-implementation, not a source of truth.' Snippet comment: 'Call with dest_v4 = 8.8.8.8.'
refuted.why_wrong:
The factual statement about what GetBestRoute2 computes is correct, but the RECOMMENDATION is wrong for LinkSwitch and I disproved it empirically on this machine. Running the dive's `winning_interface_for(8.8.8.8)` verbatim returned:
  winning ifIndex=43 routeMetric=0 prefixLen=0
  -> matches adapter: ProtonVPN   (IfType 53, WireGuard Tunnel, HardwareInterface bit = 0)
Neither Ethernet nor Wi-Fi. A LinkSwitch widget wired to this would display 'neither' — or crash a match — for every user running any full-tunnel VPN, which is a large fraction of the target audience. Cross-checked with `netstat -rn`: two 0.0.0.0/0 routes exist, Wi-Fi at effective metric 30 and the VPN at effective metric 0. GetBestRoute2 is answering a different question than the one the UI asks.

Second, related empirical finding that breaks the 'just walk the table' fallback too: Ethernet (ifIndex 4, cable currently unplugged, MediaConnectState=2) has NO 0.0.0.0/0 row in GetIpForwardTable2 at all. A route-table-derived UI cannot even enumerate Ethernet as a candidate.
refuted.correction:
Use a two-stage resolution, and drive the UI from adapter enumeration, not from the route table:

1. Enumerate adapters (GetAdaptersAddresses) and keep the ones with HardwareInterface=1 and IfType in {6,71}. These, and only these, are LinkSwitch's two rows. They persist in the UI even with no default route.
2. For 'which of MY two is currently preferred', walk GetIpForwardTable2 for PrefixLength==0, compute effective = row.Metric + GetIpInterfaceEntry(luid).Metric, and pick the lowest **among hardware interfaces only**. Verified output on this machine: Wi-Fi eff=30, ProtonVPN eff=0 -> filtering to hardware gives Wi-Fi, which is the correct answer for the widget.
3. Keep GetBestRoute2(8.8.8.8) as a SEPARATE, honestly-labelled readout ('Internet currently egresses via: ProtonVPN'). It is genuinely authoritative for that question, and surfacing the VPN is a feature — it explains to the user why toggling Ethernet/Wi-Fi did not change their apparent IP.

Do not silently present GetBestRoute2's answer as 'Ethernet' or 'Wi-Fi'.

refuted.claim: Open question 2: 'Whether to additionally special-case NET_IF_CONNECTION_TYPE (Dedicated=1 for real Ethernet vs Passive=2 for e.g. RAS/some virtual adapters) as a tertiary filter alongside HardwareInterface — worth empirically testing on the dev machine.'
refuted.why_wrong: I ran that test. NET_IF_CONNECTION_TYPE has ZERO discriminating power. Across all 10 adapters on this machine — Intel I225-V Ethernet, RZ608 Wi-Fi, Loopback Pseudo-Interface, VMware VMnet1/VMnet8, Hyper-V 'vEthernet (Default Switch)', ProtonVPN WireGuard tunnel, Bluetooth PAN, and two Microsoft Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapters — ConnectionType was 1 (NET_IF_CONNECTION_DEDICATED) for every single one, including software loopback and the WireGuard tunnel. The dive's own hedge ('Microsoft's docs don't promise virtual adapters are consistently non-Dedicated') understates it: on real hardware nothing is ever non-Dedicated.
refuted.correction: Drop NET_IF_CONNECTION_TYPE from the filter entirely; it adds a syscall and no information. The open question is closed. The HardwareInterface bit alone was perfectly discriminating on this 10-adapter sample: HW=1 for exactly {Ethernet, Wi-Fi} and HW=0 for all eight virtual/tunnel/loopback/Bluetooth/Wi-Fi-Direct adapters. Notably it correctly rejected 'Microsoft Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapter' which reports IfType=71 (IEEE80211) — strong confirmation of the dive's core point that IfType alone is insufficient.

refuted.claim: hwnic.rs trailing NOTE: 'Description-substring matching ("Virtual", "Hyper-V", "VMware", "TAP", "vEthernet", "Bluetooth", "WAN Miniport") is a useful *extra* belt-and-suspenders filter for edge cases (e.g. some USB Wi-Fi dongles or SR-IOV NICs may not set HardwareInterface consistently on older drivers).'
refuted.why_wrong: Two problems. (1) The stated justification is unsourced speculation — the dive cites nothing for 'some USB Wi-Fi dongles or SR-IOV NICs may not set HardwareInterface consistently', and I found no first-party support for it; MIB_IF_ROW2 docs define HardwareInterface flatly as 'Set if the network interface is for hardware' with no driver-version caveat. (2) More importantly the proposed fallback is actively harmful: IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH.Description and MIB_IF_ROW2.Description/Alias are LOCALIZED. On a German Windows the Hyper-V adapter is 'Hyper-V Virtueller Ethernetadapter'; the Bluetooth PAN device and 'WAN Miniport' strings are likewise translated. An English substring blacklist silently degrades to no-filter on non-English installs, and for an MIT open-source project shipped to arbitrary users that is a real defect, not belt-and-suspenders.
refuted.correction: Rely on HardwareInterface (bit 0) as the sole discriminator, as the dive's primary recommendation already says. If you want a genuine second signal, use locale-independent numeric fields already in the MIB_IF_ROW2 you fetched: MIB_IF_ROW2.PhysicalAddressLength (real NICs report 6; loopback/tunnels report 0) and NDIS_PHYSICAL_MEDIUM (PhysicalMediumType: NdisPhysicalMedium802_3=14 / NdisPhysicalMediumNative802_11=9 vs NdisPhysicalMediumUnspecified=0 for software adapters). Never branch on a user-visible string.

You do not need GetIpInterfaceEntry at all just to DISPLAY the current metrics — IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH already carries `pub Ipv4Metric: u32` and `pub Ipv6Metric: u32`, free in the enumeration you are already doing. The dive's Adapter struct omits both, which is a strange gap for a metric-steering widget. Verified they agree exactly with GetIpInterfaceEntry: Ethernet Ipv4Metric=5 vs Metric=5; Wi-Fi 30 vs 30; ProtonVPN 0 vs 0. CAVEAT I measured: Ipv6Metric read 0 for Ethernet, Wi-Fi and every adapter except loopback (75) and Hyper-V (5000) — it is not trustworthy for v6. Use Ipv4Metric from the enumeration for the v4 display, and GetIpInterfaceEntry(Family=AF_INET6) if you also steer v6.

The dive decodes 'cable still plugged in?' out of the NotMediaConnected bitfield bit, but MIB_IF_ROW2 has a plain non-bitfield enum for exactly this: `MediaConnectState: NET_IF_MEDIA_CONNECT_STATE` (0=Unknown, 1=MediaConnectStateConnected, 2=MediaConnectStateDisconnected). Measured on this machine with the Ethernet cable out: ifidx 4 MediaConnectState=2, OperStatus=2 (IfOperStatusDown), NotMediaConnected bit=1 — all three agree, but the enum is the readable one. This matters more for LinkSwitch than for most apps: the user's entire premise is 'the cable stays plugged in', so the widget must distinguish 'Ethernet deprioritized by us (metric raised, MediaConnectState=1)' from 'Ethernet actually unplugged (MediaConnectState=2)'. Those look identical if you only watch the default route.

Corollary that invalidates any route-table-driven UI: an interface whose cable is unplugged has NO 0.0.0.0/0 row whatsoever. GetIpForwardTable2(AF_INET) returned 37 rows on this machine, of which exactly two were default routes (Wi-Fi and the VPN) — Ethernet was simply absent. Build the two-row widget from GetAdaptersAddresses + HardwareInterface, and treat the route table purely as an overlay that annotates which of those rows currently wins.

NotifyRouteChange2 takes a BARE `callercontext: *const c_void`, while NotifyIpInterfaceChange and NotifyUnicastIpAddressChange take `callercontext: Option<*const c_void>`. The dive's snippet happens to get this right (it passes std::ptr::null() to one and None to the other two) but its claim text never flags the asymmetry, so anyone refactoring the three registrations into a uniform helper gets error[E0308]. Verified against the generated source at IpHelper/mod.rs:858, 876, 893.

Alignment UB in the buffer-resize loop: `align_of::<IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH>() == 8` (measured; size 448), but `Vec<u8>` guarantees only align 1. Casting `buffer.as_mut_ptr() as *mut IP_ADAPTER_ADDRESSES_LH` is technically UB and Miri flags it — it works today only because the Windows allocator happens to return 16-byte-aligned blocks for 15KB (I confirmed the pointer was 8-aligned at runtime). Cheap fix that costs nothing: allocate `let mut buffer: Vec<u64> = vec![0u64; (buf_len as usize + 7) / 8];` and cast from that, or use a `#[repr(align(8))]` newtype. Note this is also why Microsoft's own C sample uses HeapAlloc rather than a char array.

The dive flags the [T;1] flexible-array trap for WLAN_INTERFACE_INFO_LIST but not for the two IP Helper tables that have the identical problem: `MIB_IPFORWARD_TABLE2 { NumEntries: u32, Table: [MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2; 1] }` and `MIB_IF_TABLE2 { NumEntries: u32, Table: [MIB_IF_ROW2; 1] }`. Iterate with `std::slice::from_raw_parts((*tbl).Table.as_ptr(), (*tbl).NumEntries as usize)` — verified working, and note the field is `NumEntries` on these two (not `dwNumberOfItems` as on the WLAN list).

Edition-2024 note (precise, because it is easy to overstate): on rustc 1.96.1 with edition 2024 the dive's `unsafe fn sockaddr_to_ip` and `unsafe fn pwstr_to_string` bodies produce four `warning[E0133]: ... requires unsafe block` diagnostics (unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn) — WARNINGS, not errors; the crate builds. But `cargo new` defaults to edition 2024 and most projects run CI with -D warnings, so wrap the bodies in an explicit `unsafe { }` block before this bites. All five snippets otherwise compile clean against windows 0.62.2 + egui 0.36.1.

SetIpInterfaceEntry's privilege requirement is stricter than 'run elevated' and directly constrains the Task Scheduler design: the docs say it fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED unless the caller is an Administrators member AND 'the application has been marked in the manifest file with a requestedExecutionLevel set to requireAdministrator'. Since LinkSwitch is a single binary that ALSO runs unelevated as the widget, do not embed requireAdministrator in the manifest (that would force a UAC prompt on the GUI too). Register the scheduled task with RunLevel=HighestAvailable and rely on the task's elevated token — but test this specific path early, because the manifest clause is the part people get bitten by.

Read MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW.DisableDefaultRoutes and surface it. It is a BOOLEAN a VPN client can set via SetIpInterfaceEntry to kill an interface's default route outright ('can be used as a security measure by VPN clients to restrict split tunneling'). If a VPN sets it on your Ethernet or Wi-Fi interface, metric steering will appear to do nothing at all and the user will file a bug against LinkSwitch. Measured false on all three interfaces I checked here, but it costs one field of the row you are already fetching. Same read also gives you `Connected: bool` (measured: Ethernet false, Wi-Fi true, VPN true).

Windows 10+ behaviour change that quietly validates the whole design: 'Starting with Windows 10, the order in which adapters appear in the list [from GetAdaptersAddresses] is determined by the IPv4 or IPv6 route metric.' So on Win10/11 the enumeration order itself already reflects metric preference — useful as a free sanity check that your metric write took effect, but never depend on it for correctness, and never assume Ethernet-before-Wi-Fi ordering.

No networking, registry or scheduled-task state was modified; probe3 uses GetIpForwardTable2 + FreeMibTable and GetIfEntry2, all read-only, and was cross-validated against `netstat -rn`.

dive.topic: egui/eframe desktop-widget shell on Windows 11 for LinkSwitch
dive.summary:
eframe/egui are both at 0.36.1 (crates.io, released 2026-08-07), released in lockstep. eframe now defaults to wgpu (feature "wgpu" default-on, "glow" default-off; other defaults: accesskit, default_fonts, wayland, x11, web_screen_reader, links). "persistence" is opt-in.

ViewportBuilder covers every knob: with_decorations(false), with_transparent(true), with_always_on_top() (sugar for with_window_level(WindowLevel::AlwaysOnTop)), with_taskbar(false) (Windows-only; internally -> WindowAttributesExtWindows::with_skip_taskbar(true) -> WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW, which removes both taskbar AND Alt-Tab entries), with_inner_size/with_min_inner_size, with_resizable(false), with_position. When decorations=false and fullscreen=false, eframe's Windows path auto-calls with_undecorated_shadow(true) — a real OS drop shadow appears around the undecorated window for free (verified in egui-winit's create_winit_window_attributes). There is NO built-in resize grip for undecorated viewports: the official custom_window_frame example (verified against emilk/egui main) implements only StartDrag, never resizing; resize needs manual edge/corner hit-testing + ViewportCommand::BeginResize(ResizeDirection::{North,South,East,West,NorthEast,NorthWest,SouthEast,SouthWest}). Drag-with-clickable-buttons is solved exactly as in that example: ui.interact(rect, id, Sense::click_and_drag()) over the background, drag_started_by(PointerButton::Primary) -> send_viewport_cmd(StartDrag), then real buttons added afterward in a nested scope over the same rect still receive their own clicks.

Idle CPU: eframe is reactive by default (ControlFlow::Wait, or ControlFlow::WaitUntil(next_repaint_time) after request_repaint_after) — verified directly in eframe's native/run.rs source. A widget that never requests repaint sits fully blocked (near-0% CPU). A historical minimized-window CPU bug (#3982, up to 17%) is mitigated in current code via an explicit 10ms sleep when the window is invisible/minimized. A still-open winit issue (#1610) claims WaitUntil can misbehave on some Windows 10 configs — must be empirically verified on real hardware.

DPI: winit already calls SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) automatically before any window is created, so a plain eframe app is already Per-Monitor-V2 aware with zero manifest. A manifest is still recommended (Microsoft's own guidance prefers manifest over the runtime API) and is needed anyway to pin requestedExecutionLevel="asInvoker" explicitly (critical: must NOT be highestAvailable/requireAdministrator, or the widget UAC-prompts on every plain launch, breaking the whole one-time-elevation design) and to suppress the legacy filename-based installer-elevation heuristic. embed-manifest's new_manifest() defaults to exactly AsInvoker + PerMonitorV2 + Win7-11 supportedOS — a one-line drop-in.

Tray icon: tray-icon 0.24.2 is current. On Windows the icon must be built on the main thread after the winit event loop has started; the correct place is inside the eframe app-creator closure passed to run_native (verified against tray-icon's own maintained examples/egui.rs, current on the dev branch). tray-icon's Windows backend already registers for and re-handles WM_TASKBARCREATED internally (including a ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx UIPI allowance so an elevated app can still re-register after explorer.exe restarts), so the classic "tray icon vanishes after explorer restart" bug is pre-solved. Icon::from_resource(ordinal, None) can load the icon straight out of the exe's own embedded .ico resource (no separate image decode needed). The single biggest real gotcha (from emilk/egui discussion #737): fully hiding the window via ViewportCommand::Visible(false) can stop egui from calling App::update() at all, so the app never sees the tray-restore click. The verified workaround is to bypass eframe's viewport visibility entirely — grab the raw HWND once via Frame::window_handle() (raw-window-handle, no extra feature) and hide/show with a direct windows-rs ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE/SW_SHOW) + SetForegroundWindow call, while keeping ctx.request_repaint_after(short duration) running so the loop keeps polling TrayIconEvent::receiver() while "hidden."

Console: a GUI-subsystem exe's std::io::stdout()/stderr() get a null handle and silently no-op — confirmed by rust-lang/rust's own stdio docs. Fix for the single-binary design: at the very top of main(), before any output, when argv indicates a CLI subcommand, call windows-rs AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS), then explicitly SetStdHandle for STD_OUTPUT/ERROR/INPUT_HANDLE with fresh handles from CreateFileW("CONOUT$"/"CONIN$", ...) — AttachConsole alone does not repair the process's already-fixed inherited std handles. Needs three windows-rs features that are NOT auto-pulled by each other: Win32_Foundation, Win32_System_Console, Win32_Storage_FileSystem (verified against windows-rs 0.62.0's own Cargo.toml feature-dependency graph).

Persistence: recommend a single hand-rolled JSON file (serde_json) under %APPDATA%\LinkSwitch\, not eframe's built-in "persistence" feature/RON storage — because --apply and --install-tasks never call eframe::run_native at all and so can never reach eframe's Storage machinery; one config file readable by every subcommand is simpler than splitting window-position RON state from app config JSON.

claims.claim: eframe and egui both have max_stable_version 0.36.1 on crates.io, published 2026-08-07.
eframe's default Cargo features include accesskit, default_fonts, wayland, web_screen_reader, wgpu, wgpu_no_default_features, x11, links; glow and persistence are NOT default.

NativeOptions fields: viewport, multisampling, depth_buffer, stencil_buffer, renderer, run_and_return (default true), event_loop_builder, window_builder, centered, persist_window, glow_options, wgpu_options, persistence_path, dithering (default true). There is no top-level vsync field (it lives inside GlowConfiguration/WgpuConfiguration).

ViewportBuilder has (among others) fields: title, app_id, position, inner_size, min_inner_size, max_inner_size, resizable, transparent, decorations, icon, active, visible, and Windows-specific drag_and_drop, taskbar, close_button, minimize_button, maximize_button, window_level, mouse_passthrough.

eframe's egui-winit Windows codepath maps ViewportBuilder::taskbar to WindowAttributesExtWindows::with_skip_taskbar(!show) -> WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW, and separately auto-sets with_undecorated_shadow(!decorations && !fullscreen), giving an OS drop shadow on undecorated windows automatically.
ResizeDirection enum has variants North, South, East, West, NorthEast, SouthEast, NorthWest, SouthWest, used with ViewportCommand::BeginResize.

The official emilk/egui example examples/custom_window_frame/src/main.rs implements title-bar dragging via ui.interact(...).drag_started_by(PointerButton::Primary) -> send_viewport_cmd(ViewportCommand::StartDrag), and does NOT implement any resize-border logic at all.

eframe's native run loop sets winit's ControlFlow to WaitUntil(next_repaint_time) when a repaint was scheduled (via request_repaint_after) and to Wait otherwise; current source also sleeps 10ms in a loop when the window is invisible or minimized to cap CPU use.

egui issue #3982 documented up to 17% idle CPU when an eframe window was minimized on Windows 10, regressed vs egui 0.25, with a fix PR (#3985) linked; the issue itself remains open on GitHub as of the check.

winit issue #1610 (ControlFlow::WaitUntil causing high CPU specifically on Windows 10) exists with a referenced fix PR #3950; current resolution status for the exact winit version in use was not confirmed from available content.

Window transparency on Windows in eframe has two still-open GitHub issues as of the check: #4451 (glow backend renders solid black instead of transparent) and #5512 (a Cargo package literally named "overlay" triggers a black background bug); issue #2680 (wgpu transparency) was closed back in 2023.

winit automatically calls SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) on Windows before creating any window, falling back to older APIs on Windows 8.1, meaning eframe apps are already Per-Monitor-V2 DPI aware without any manifest.
claims.source: search-derived from winit source discussion; corroborated by Microsoft Learn guidance that SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext must be called before any HWND is created

claims.claim: embed-manifest crate is at version 1.5.0 (2026-09-01); its new_manifest() builder defaults to ExecutionLevel::AsInvoker, DpiAwareness::PerMonitorV2, and a Windows 7 through 11 supportedOS list, with a one-call build.rs usage: embed_manifest(new_manifest("id")).unwrap() gated on CARGO_CFG_WINDOWS.

embed-manifest embeds ONLY the manifest; it does not embed an .ico application icon. Icon embedding still requires embed-resource (3.0.11, current) or winres/winresource with a small .rc file (e.g. `1 ICON "app.ico"`) compiled via embed_resource::compile(...).manifest_optional().

tray-icon crate current version is 0.24.2 (2026-07-27). On Windows and Linux, an event loop must already be running on the same thread the tray icon is created on (a win32 message loop on Windows, gtk main loop on Linux); on macOS it must be the main thread.

tray-icon's Windows backend (platform_impl/windows/mod.rs) registers the "TaskbarCreated" window message via RegisterWindowMessageA and calls ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx(hwnd, taskbar_created_msg, MSGFLT_ALLOW, ...) specifically so an elevated process can still receive that broadcast from a non-elevated explorer.exe and re-register its icon after Explorer restarts.

tray_icon::Icon has constructors from_rgba, and (Windows-only, #[cfg(windows)]) from_path, from_resource(ordinal: u16, size: Option<(u32,u32)>), from_resource_name, from_handle(handle: isize) — from_resource loads an icon directly out of the running exe's own embedded Win32 resources.

The maintained tray-icon example for eframe (examples/egui.rs on the tauri-apps/tray-icon dev branch) constructs the TrayIcon on non-Linux platforms strictly inside the Box::new(move |_cc| {...}) app-creator closure passed to eframe::run_native, and polls TrayIconEvent::receiver().try_recv() once per App::update() call.

In emilk/egui discussion #737, community consensus is that ViewportCommand::Visible(false) can stop egui from calling App::update() at all while the viewport is not interactable, which would starve a tray-restore click of any chance to be seen; the workaround used in practice is to hide/show the window via a direct win32 ShowWindow call on the raw HWND instead of the ViewportCommand, tracked with an external flag.

eframe::Frame::window_handle() -> Result<raw_window_handle::WindowHandle<'_>, HandleError> is available on native (non-wasm) targets with no extra Cargo feature required, implementing raw_window_handle::HasWindowHandle; on Windows its RawWindowHandle::Win32 variant exposes the HWND.

A Windows GUI-subsystem process's inherited standard handles are fixed at process creation; calling windows::Win32::System::Console::AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) alone does not repair std::io::stdout()/stderr(), which read a null handle and silently no-op writes on such processes — you must additionally call SetStdHandle with new handles opened via CreateFileW("CONOUT$"/"CONIN$", ...) before the first use of println!/stdout().
claims.source: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/9486 and https://www.tillett.info/2013/05/13/how-to-create-a-windows-program-that-works-as-both-as-a-gui-and-console-application/ (C/C++ freopen analogue of the same handle problem)

claims.claim: windows-rs 0.62.0's published Cargo.toml declares Win32_System_Console = ["Win32_System"] and Win32_Storage_FileSystem = ["Win32_Storage"] — neither transitively pulls in Win32_Foundation, so code using HANDLE types returned by CreateFileW/passed to SetStdHandle must explicitly also enable the Win32_Foundation feature.
windows::Win32::System::Console::AttachConsole has signature pub unsafe fn AttachConsole(dwprocessid: u32) -> windows::core::Result<()>, gated by the Win32_System_Console Cargo feature.

eframe::storage_dir(app_id) resolves on Windows to %APPDATA%\<app_id>\data (Roaming AppData), and eframe's built-in persistence stores app state as RON at that path when NativeOptions::persist_window / the App::save mechanism is used with the "persistence" feature enabled.

code.purpose: Cargo.toml dependency block for the LinkSwitch widget shell (Windows-only, wgpu renderer, custom JSON persistence, tray icon, raw win32 access for console/HWND tricks)
code.snippet:
[package]
name = "linkswitch"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
build = "build.rs"

[dependencies]
# eframe's defaults already include wgpu + default_fonts + accesskit + wayland + x11 + web_screen_reader + links.
# Trim wayland/x11 since this is Windows-only; keep persistence OFF (see §8 rationale) unless you decide
# you specifically want eframe's own window-position RON store instead of your own JSON.
eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false, features = ["wgpu", "default_fonts", "accesskit"] }
egui  = "0.36"

tray-icon = "0.24"

serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"

raw-window-handle = "0.6"   # re-exported by eframe too; pin explicitly for the HWND extraction snippet

windows = { version = "0.62", features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_System_Console",          # AttachConsole/SetStdHandle for --apply/--install-tasks output
    "Win32_Storage_FileSystem",      # CreateFileW("CONOUT$"/"CONIN$")
    "Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging",  # ShowWindow/SetForegroundWindow for hide-to-tray
] }

[build-dependencies]
embed-manifest  = "1.5"   # dpiAware=PerMonitorV2 + requestedExecutionLevel=asInvoker, one call
embed-resource  = "3.0"   # embeds the .ico via a tiny .rc file

code.purpose: build.rs: embed manifest (DPI + asInvoker) and the .ico icon in one build script
assets/app.rc -- icon-only resource script (resource id 1 is reused later by tray_icon::Icon::from_resource(1, ...))
code.snippet: 1 ICON "app.ico"

code.purpose: NativeOptions / ViewportBuilder setup for the borderless, transparent, always-on-top, tool-window widget
Drag-the-whole-body-but-still-click-buttons pattern, adapted directly from emilk/egui's official custom_window_frame example
Optional manual resize handling -- NOT built in; only implement if the widget must be resizable
Idle-CPU-correct update loop: never repaint unless something actually changed; poll adapter state on a slow timer instead of every frame
Tray icon integration adapted from tray-icon's own maintained eframe example (dev branch), using Icon::from_resource so no separate PNG/image crate is needed on Windows
Hide-to-tray / restore that bypasses ViewportCommand::Visible (which can stop App::update from firing per egui discussion #737) by driving the raw HWND directly
Console visibility for the single binary's --apply/--install-tasks/--uninstall-tasks subcommands, while the no-args GUI launch stays windowless (windows_subsystem="windows")
Hand-rolled JSON persistence shared by the GUI, --apply, and --install-tasks code paths (recommended over eframe's built-in persistence feature)

gotchas: Window transparency on Windows has two still-OPEN eframe/egui GitHub issues as of this research (#4451: glow backend renders solid black instead of transparent; #5512: a crate/package literally named "overlay" triggers a black background). Build a minimal transparent-window repro FIRST, on the actual target machine/GPU driver, before investing in the rest of the widget -- don't assume with_transparent(true) just works. Prefer the wgpu renderer (now eframe's default) over glow for this reason.

with_taskbar(false) / with_always_on_top() / with_decorations(false) are only meaningful on native desktop; with_taskbar is Windows-specific (WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW) and has no effect on other platforms -- fine here since this is a Windows-only project, but don't copy this ViewportBuilder verbatim into a cross-platform doc example without noting that.

Do NOT set requestedExecutionLevel to highestAvailable or requireAdministrator in the embedded manifest. That would make Windows UAC-prompt on every single plain launch of linkswitch.exe (including the no-args widget launch and the Task-Scheduler-triggered --apply runs), defeating the entire one-time-elevation design. embed-manifest's new_manifest() defaults to asInvoker already -- just don't override it.

ViewportCommand::Visible(false) can stop egui from calling App::update() at all while the viewport is considered non-interactable (per emilk/egui discussion #737), which would make a tray-icon restore-click invisible to the app forever. Hide/restore via a direct win32 ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE/SW_SHOW) call on the raw HWND (from Frame::window_handle()) instead, and keep a short ctx.request_repaint_after() ticking while "hidden" so the tray channel keeps getting polled. Treat this as the riskiest, least-officially-documented corner of the whole shell and validate it manually early.

AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) alone does not make println!/eprintln! work again on a windows_subsystem="windows" binary -- Rust's std::io::stdout()/stderr() read a null handle on such processes and silently no-op writes. You must also SetStdHandle with fresh CreateFileW("CONOUT$"/"CONIN$") handles, and do all of this before the very first stdout/stderr use in main().

windows-rs feature flags do not transitively imply Win32_Foundation: Win32_System_Console = ["Win32_System"] and Win32_Storage_FileSystem = ["Win32_Storage"] in the crate's own Cargo.toml (verified at the 0.62.0 tag), so any code touching a raw HANDLE (e.g. from CreateFileW, or passed to SetStdHandle) needs Win32_Foundation listed explicitly too, or it fails to compile with a confusing type-not-found error.

Task Scheduler launches the --apply worker with no console at all (and often no working parent process to attach to), so AttachConsole will simply fail there -- design --apply's diagnostics around a log file (e.g. also under %APPDATA%\LinkSwitch\), not around console output, and only rely on AttachConsole for the interactive --install-tasks/--uninstall-tasks path run by a human from a terminal.

eframe's own built-in persistence (the "persistence" Cargo feature + NativeOptions::persist_window + storage_dir()) is only reachable from inside code that actually calls eframe::run_native. The --apply and --install-tasks code paths in this project's single binary never call run_native, so they structurally cannot read or write eframe's persisted state -- a shared hand-rolled JSON file is not just a style preference here, it's close to a requirement if config needs to be visible to every subcommand.

The tray icon MUST be constructed on the same OS thread that is pumping the win32 message loop, and specifically after that loop has started -- concretely, inside the Box::new(move |cc| ...) app-creator closure passed to eframe::run_native, not before calling run_native. tray-icon itself already re-registers after explorer.exe restarts (WM_TASKBARCREATED handling with a UIPI allowance baked into its Windows backend), so you do not need to reimplement that part yourself.

There is genuinely no built-in resize handle/grip for an undecorated egui viewport -- confirmed by reading the official custom_window_frame example in full, which implements dragging only. If LinkSwitch's widget can be a fixed-size box (likely, given it's a toggle control), simply skip resizing (with_resizable(false)) rather than reimplementing BeginResize edge-hit-testing, which is nontrivial to get feeling right (cursor icons, corner vs edge priority, minimum-size clamping).

Build a minimal with_transparent(true) + with_decorations(false) + Renderer::Wgpu repro FIRST and visually confirm rounded corners + drop shadow render correctly (no black fill, no square-shadow-behind-rounded-content mismatch) on the actual target GPU/driver -- issues #4451 and #5512 are open and unresolved upstream, so this cannot be assumed to just work from documentation alone.

Validate the ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)-bypasses-eframe's-visibility-tracking hide-to-tray technique end-to-end: does the winit/eframe event loop keep calling App::update() (via our own request_repaint_after ticks) while the HWND is hidden this way, and does restore (SW_SHOW + SetForegroundWindow) reliably bring the window back both visually and to keyboard focus on Windows 11 specifically (behavior here is community-folklore from a GitHub discussion, not an officially documented eframe/egui contract).

Confirm the exact current eframe/egui-winit dependency versions of winit and raw-window-handle bundled with eframe 0.36.1 (not independently re-verified in this pass) match the raw_window_handle 0.6.x Win32WindowHandle.hwnd: NonZeroIsize shape assumed in the HWND-extraction snippet -- a Cargo.lock check once the project is scaffolded will settle this in seconds.

Decide whether the widget needs any resizing at all; if a future requirement calls for it, prototype the manual BeginResize edge/corner hit-testing (cursor icon swapping included) early since there is no reference implementation to copy from the official examples.

refuted.why_wrong:
Refuted empirically on this machine and by Microsoft's own doc. I built a `#![windows_subsystem="windows"]` probe with windows 0.62.2 and ran it under two launch modes (PowerShell Start-Process; `cmd /c start "" /wait`). Identical results both times:
```
pre  GetStdHandle = Err(...)          <- NULL handle, as expected

post GetStdHandle = 0xac, GetFileType = 2   <- FILE_TYPE_CHAR (a console)

rust stdout write = Ok(26)

```

note: found an item that was configured out
  windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/Storage/FileSystem/mod.rs:361

refuted.claim: "You must also SetStdHandle ... and do all of this before the very first stdout/stderr use in main()." / "Re-point them BEFORE the first println!/eprintln! call".

Rust's std re-reads GetStdHandle on each write; there is no cached handle to poison. Empirical probe (GUI-subsystem exe, launched with stdout redirected to a file):
```rust
println!("BEFORE_ATTACH"); stdout().flush();      // forces std's lazy stdout to init AND write
SetStdHandle(STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE, <handle to redirect_probe.txt>);
println!("AFTER_SETSTDHANDLE"); stdout().flush();
```
Result: `direct_stdout.txt` contained only `BEFORE_ATTACH`; `redirect_probe.txt` contained `AFTER_SETSTDHANDLE`. SetStdHandle took effect retroactively after stdout had already been initialized and written to.
refuted.correction: Ordering is not load-bearing. The only real ordering concern is unflushed bytes already sitting in `Stdout`'s LineWriter buffer, which will flush to whatever handle is current at flush time. Don't build the argv-dispatch design around a constraint that doesn't exist.
