added_gotchas: TRAY CLICKS ARE INVISIBLE TO A REACTIVE APP IF YOU ONLY POLL. `TrayIconEvent::receiver().try_recv()` inside `App::ui`/`logic` only runs when eframe decides to tick. A correctly idle widget (never calls request_repaint) sits blocked in ControlFlow::Wait and will never observe the click. Push instead of poll, ONCE at startup: `tray_icon::TrayIconEvent::set_event_handler(Some(move |ev| { let _ = tx.send(ev); ctx.request_repaint(); }))` where `ctx` is a cloned `egui::Context` (it is Send+Sync+cheap-clone) captured from `CreationContext`. Two traps in that API (tray-icon-0.24.2/src/lib.rs:684): it is backed by a `OnceLock`, so it can be set exactly once and never changed; and once set, `TrayIconEvent::receiver()` receives NOTHING (`send()` routes to the handler OR the channel, never both). Same pattern applies to `muda::MenuEvent::set_event_handler` if you add a tray context menu.

`run_and_return: true` (the default, epi.rs:342) makes eframe use `EventLoopExtRunOnDemand`, so `run_native` RETURNS when the window closes and the win32 message pump stops — which kills the tray icon's message-only window along with it. For hide-to-tray, never send `ViewportCommand::Close` on the 'X' button; send `ViewportCommand::Visible(false)`. Reserve Close for a real Quit item on the tray menu.

windows-rs `GetStdHandle` reports a NULL handle as `Err(Error { code: HRESULT(0x00000000), message: "The operation completed successfully." })` — a success-coded error. I hit this in the probe. Don't log-and-panic on it, and don't read the message string as meaningful; check `.is_err()` or compare against a null HANDLE.

`Icon::from_resource(1, None)` resolves to `LoadImageW(hinst, MAKEINTRESOURCE(1), IMAGE_ICON, 0, 0, LR_DEFAULTSIZE)` (tray-icon platform_impl/windows/icon.rs:112-130). Per learn.microsoft.com LoadImageW: cx/cy of 0 with LR_DEFAULTSIZE means "the function uses the SM_CXICON / SM_CYICON system metric value" — i.e. the LARGE icon (32px at 100% DPI), not the notification-area size, and not `LoadIconMetric(LIM_SMALL)` which Microsoft's notification-area guidance recommends for DPI correctness. Microsoft does say supplying an SM_CXICON-sized icon and letting the shell scale it down is acceptable, so `None` is defensible — but if the tray icon looks soft on a 150%-scaled Win11 display, pass `Some((w,h))` from `GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSMICON/SM_CYSMICON)`. Also note there is no LR_SHARED, and `RaiiIcon::drop` calls `DestroyIcon` — so keep the `TrayIcon` alive; dropping it destroys the HICON.

In windows-rs 0.62.x a function is gated on the feature of EVERY namespace in its signature, not just its own module. Beyond the dive's Win32_Foundation point, I confirmed by compile error: `CreateFileW` needs `Win32_Security` (SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES param) and `WriteFile` needs `Win32_System_IO` (OVERLAPPED param). The error is always E0432 'no `X` in `Y`' plus a helpful `note: found an item that was configured out ... gated behind the "Z" feature` — read the note, it names the exact feature.

`App::ui`'s rustdoc: "The given egui::Ui has no margin or background color. You can wrap your UI code in egui::CentralPanel or a egui::Frame::central_panel to remedy this." If you port the dive's code by mechanically renaming `update`→`ui` and keeping a bare Ui, you get an unpainted transparent void — which, on a `with_transparent(true)` widget, looks exactly like the #4451 'black/invisible window' bug you were told to hunt for. Rule out this self-inflicted case before blaming the renderer.

The `custom_window_frame` example at tag 0.36.1 makes only the 32px title bar draggable, not the whole body. The dive's whole-body `Sense::click_and_drag()` variant compiles and works, but note the interaction order that makes it work: `ui.interact(body_rect, ...)` must come BEFORE the `scope_builder` that adds the buttons — later widgets win egui's interaction contest. Reversing those two statements silently breaks every button.

winit's `set_skip_taskbar` runs `com_initialized()` (CoInitializeEx on the event-loop thread) at window creation, and tray-icon's Windows backend runs on that same thread. If you later add anything else COM-based to the widget thread, you inherit winit's apartment choice rather than picking your own — don't call CoInitializeEx yourself with a conflicting apartment model on that thread.

`eframe::storage_dir(app_id)` on Windows is `roaming_appdata()/<app_id>/data` (native/file_storage.rs:37) — note the trailing `data` segment, so it is `%APPDATA%\LinkSwitch\data`, NOT `%APPDATA%\LinkSwitch`. If you ever compare or migrate paths against the dive's recommended hand-rolled `%APPDATA%\LinkSwitch\config.json`, they are siblings, not the same directory. The dive's recommendation to hand-roll JSON is otherwise sound and I'd keep it — `--apply` and `--install-tasks` genuinely never call `run_native`.
verification.verdict: NOT trustworthy as written — the factual inventory is good but the code is written against the wrong eframe version, so an implementer copying it hits a wall immediately. Roughly 23 claims survived verification (crate versions, ViewportBuilder field list, ResizeDirection, NativeOptions shape and defaults, the taskbar/undecorated-shadow call sites existing at all, reactive Wait/WaitUntil, transparency issues #4451/#5512 open and #2680 closed, winit's automatic PMv2 DPI call, embed-manifest/embed-resource split, tray-icon's WM_TASKBARCREATED + ChangeWindowMessageFilterEx UIPI handling, the Icon constructor list, Frame::window_handle, the non-transitive Win32_Foundation rule, AttachConsole's signature, and the hand-rolled-JSON-over-eframe-persistence reasoning). But three failures are structural, not cosmetic. (1) Every Rust snippet targets `eframe::App::update`, which does not exist in the eframe 0.36 the dive itself pins — verified by cargo: E0407 + E0046 + E0308. The trait is now `logic()` + `ui(&mut Ui, ...)`. (2) The dive's self-declared \"riskiest corner\" — the ViewportCommand::Visible(false) tray gotcha and its raw-ShowWindow workaround — was fixed upstream on 2026-03-24 (egui #5229, #7776) and eframe 0.36.1 ships a purpose-built `App::logic()` hidden-window tick for exactly this; worse, the recommended workaround permanently desyncs winit's cached VISIBLE flag so `Visible(true)` becomes a silent no-op. (3) The Cargo.toml does not compile the console snippet (`CreateFileW` is behind `Win32_Security`) — and the console snippet is unnecessary anyway, since I measured AttachConsole alone repairing the std handles, as Microsoft's own doc states. Two of the five open questions (winit #1610, the rwh_06/NonZeroIsize shape) are already settled and should be struck. Pattern to watch: the dive read emilk/egui `main` and stale docs.rs prose while claiming to verify against the pinned version, and reported closed GitHub issues as open in three places. Use its inventory as a checklist; re-derive all code against the 0.36.1 tarball.

added_gotchas: schtasks.exe /Run CANNOT pass arguments. $(Arg0)..$(Arg32) substitution is only fed by IRegisteredTask::Run / RunEx params (max 32 strings). Verified on learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/taskschd/nf-taskschd-iregisteredtask-run. Consequence for LinkSwitch: do NOT design one parameterized task. Register THREE fixed tasks -- LinkSwitch\ApplyEthernet, LinkSwitch\ApplyWifi, LinkSwitch\ApplyAuto -- each with a hardcoded IExecAction arguments string ('--apply ethernet' etc.). This also removes an injection surface: a parameterized task lets any medium-IL process on the box feed arbitrary argv to your elevated worker.

Corollary security gotcha: whatever you put in the elevated task's action is a medium-IL-to-high-IL bridge for EVERY process running as that user. Keep the action a fixed path + fixed args to your own signed exe, install the exe under %ProgramFiles%\LinkSwitch (ACL'd so medium IL cannot write it), and never point the task at cmd.exe/powershell.exe or at a path under %LOCALAPPDATA% (user-writable => trivial escalation). Have --apply read config only from the ProgramFiles-side config, not from a user-writable path.

MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW.SitePrefixLength must be forced to 0 for IPv4 before SetIpInterfaceEntry. GetIpInterfaceEntry returns 255 (documented as 'commonly used to represent an illegal value'); passing it straight back gives ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER. Verbatim from learn.microsoft.com/.../nf-netioapi-setipinterfaceentry: 'However for IPv4, an application must not try to modify the SitePrefixLength member... For IPv4, the SitePrefixLength member must be set to 0.' This is the single most common cause of a metric-setting tool failing at 87.

SetIpInterfaceEntry in windows 0.62.2 is `pub unsafe fn SetIpInterfaceEntry(row: *mut MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW) -> WIN32_ERROR` -- it returns WIN32_ERROR, NOT windows::core::Result<()>. There is no `?` to apply and no HRESULT. You must compare against NO_ERROR / ERROR_SUCCESS yourself (e.g. `if rc != NO_ERROR { return Err(...) }`). Same for GetIpInterfaceEntry. Any snippet that writes `SetIpInterfaceEntry(&mut row)?` does not compile.

To flip a metric: set row.Family (AF_INET / AF_INET6) + row.InterfaceLuid (preferred; InterfaceIndex is explicitly documented as non-persistent and 'may change when a network adapter is disabled and then enabled'), call GetIpInterfaceEntry, then set row.UseAutomaticMetric = FALSE and row.Metric = n, zero SitePrefixLength, then SetIpInterfaceEntry. 'auto' mode = set UseAutomaticMetric = TRUE (Metric is then ignored). Persist the interface by LUID in config, not by index and not by friendly name.

IPv4 and IPv6 are SEPARATE rows. One SetIpInterfaceEntry call on AF_INET does not steer IPv6 traffic, and on a dual-stack Windows 11 box with IPv6 on Wi-Fi and Ethernet the user will see 'it didn't switch' because the browser used IPv6 via the unchanged interface. LinkSwitch must apply the metric to both AF_INET and AF_INET6 for each interface, and tolerate ERROR_NOT_FOUND on the family a given adapter has disabled (docs: ERROR_NOT_FOUND is returned when the interface 'does not match the IP address family specified in the Family member').

docs.rs does NOT host browsable docs for the windows crate's Win32 modules -- https://docs.rs/windows/0.62.2/windows/Win32/System/TaskScheduler/index.html is a hard 404 (verified), because docs.rs cannot build the crate with all features. The authoritative rendered API is https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/Win32/... . If the original dive claimed to have 'verified against docs.rs' for these namespaces, it did not open the page it says it did.

Current windows crate is 0.62.2 (crates.io, 2025-10-06). Features needed here: Win32_System_TaskScheduler, Win32_System_Com (CoInitializeEx/CoCreateInstance/COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED), Win32_System_Variant (VARIANT and VARIANT_BOOL live in windows::Win32::System::Variant, NOT in ::System::Com -- pre-0.52 blog snippets get this wrong), Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper, Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis (NET_LUID_LH), Win32_Foundation. BSTR is windows::core::BSTR (no feature).

Task Scheduler defaults are hostile to a click-to-toggle widget and MUST be overridden explicitly on ITaskSettings: DisallowStartIfOnBatteries and StopIfGoingOnBatteries (schema default true) -> set VARIANT_FALSE, or the widget silently does nothing on an unplugged laptop, which is precisely the scenario where a user switches to Wi-Fi. Also set MultipleInstances to TASK_INSTANCES_PARALLEL (0) or QUEUE (1); the schema default IgnoreNew (2) silently drops a second click while the first worker is still running. Also set a short ExecutionTimeLimit -- learn.microsoft states 'By default, a task will be stopped 72 hours after it starts to run.' Leave RunOnlyIfNetworkAvailable false (setting it true would deadlock the very feature). Leave AllowDemandStart true (required for IRegisteredTask::Run).

On battery saver specifically, ITaskSettings remarks say tasks are triggered only if the task 'Is set to Run only when user is logged on (task LogonType is TASK_LOGON_INTERACTIVE_TOKEN or TASK_LOGON_GROUP)'. This is an independent reason to use TASK_LOGON_INTERACTIVE_TOKEN rather than TASK_LOGON_S4U or a SYSTEM principal.

IRegisteredTask::Run is fire-and-forget: it returns an IRunningTask, not the worker's exit code. The widget cannot know whether the switch succeeded from the Run call. Poll IRegisteredTask::LastTaskResult (and State) after the run, or better, have --apply write a small JSON result file that the widget reads; and re-read the actual interface metrics via GetIpInterfaceTable to display truth rather than intent. Expect a few hundred ms of scheduler latency, so do not block the egui frame on it.

The task action stores an absolute exe path. If the user moves or reinstalls LinkSwitch, the task silently fails with LastTaskResult 2147942402 (0x80070002, ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND) and the widget's button appears to do nothing. On startup, compare the registered task's action Path against std::env::current_exe() and prompt for a one-time elevated re-install if they differ.

Do not detect 'am I admin' by enumerating group SIDs. Verified empirically on this machine: [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Groups reported S-1-5-32-544 absent (InAdminsGroup=False), while `whoami /groups` shows 'BUILTIN\Administrators ... Group used for deny only' at Medium Mandatory Level -- i.e. the user IS an admin, just filtered. Use GetTokenInformation(TokenElevation) for 'am I elevated now' and CheckTokenMembership with a TokenLinkedToken (or simply attempt the elevated install and handle failure) for 'could I elevate'.

SetIpInterfaceEntry's own docs warn about the built-in-Administrator/manifest interaction: 'this call will fail unless the application has been marked in the manifest file with a requestedExecutionLevel set to requireAdministrator.' Since LinkSwitch is a single binary that must ALSO run unelevated as the widget, you must NOT embed requireAdministrator in the exe manifest -- do it the other way: manifest asInvoker, and get elevation for --install-tasks via ShellExecuteEx with lpVerb="runas" (windows::Win32::UI::Shell::ShellExecuteExW, feature Win32_UI_Shell) re-launching the same exe. The scheduled task path then supplies the elevated token for --apply. Verify empirically that SetIpInterfaceEntry succeeds under the HIGHEST task even with an asInvoker manifest before building the UI on top of it -- that is the one assumption in this design worth testing first.

If UAC is disabled on the machine, RunLevel is ignored entirely (both cited pages say so). On such a box every process already runs high-IL and the design degenerates harmlessly, but the install-time 'am I elevated' check must not assume UAC exists.

Task folder naming: create a dedicated folder via ITaskFolder::CreateFolder(&BSTR::from("\\LinkSwitch"), &VARIANT::default()) and register into it, so --uninstall-tasks can delete the folder cleanly. CreateFolder returns HRESULT 0x800700B7 (ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS) on re-install -- treat that as success, not an error.

dive.topic: Does Windows 11 interface-metric steering actually deliver "switch to Wi-Fi without unplugging Ethernet"? (adversarial validation, incl. WcmSvc/fMinimizeConnections)
dive.summary:
VERDICT: metric steering works for routing, but it is NOT sufficient on its own. LinkSwitch must ALSO neutralize Windows Connection Manager, or the Wi-Fi leg will not exist to switch to.

Routing (works): Windows picks a route by longest-prefix match, then lowest TOTAL metric = route metric + interface metric (MS docs, verbatim). DHCP default routes carry RouteMetric 0 (verified locally), so interface metric alone decides. Raising Ethernet's IPv4+IPv6 interface metric above Wi-Fi's makes new connections egress Wi-Fi while Ethernet stays enabled, linked-up and addressed. Windows Vista+ uses the STRONG host model by default (WeakHostSend/Receive = FALSE, verified locally), so an unbound socket's source address follows the chosen interface — there is no RFC 6724 "wrong source address" leak. Sockets that explicitly bind to the Ethernet IP still egress Ethernet, by design.

THE KILLER (Q6): WcmSvc's "Minimize the number of simultaneous connections" policy is ON BY DEFAULT. I proved the effective default empirically on this machine (Windows 11 Education 10.0.26200, policy value absent from the registry) by P/Invoking WcmQueryProperty(wcm_global_property_minimize_policy): fValue = 1, fIsGroupPolicy = 0. Value 1 means "any new AUTOMATIC internet connection is blocked when the computer has at least one active internet connection to a preferred type of network... Ethernet is always preferred when connected" (local WCM.adml, verbatim). Consequences: after any boot/resume with the cable plugged, Wi-Fi will NOT auto-connect, so the widget's Wi-Fi button has no link to steer to; and an already-connected Wi-Fi is a soft-disconnect candidate that drops once traffic falls below threshold (checked every 30 s). Critically, MS states WCM's keep/drop decision is made from a fixed preference order (Ethernet > WLAN > cellular) and explicitly "not for routing" and never from link speed — so raising Ethernet's metric gives Wi-Fi ZERO protection. Mandatory fix: elevated write of HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WcmSvc\GroupPolicy!fMinimizeConnections = REG_DWORD 0 ("Allow simultaneous connections"). The ADML confirms the knock-on: "if 'Minimize the number of simultaneous connections...' is disabled, Windows will not disconnect from any networks." Note the ADMX enum has no disabledValue — you must WRITE 0, not delete the value.

Second real leak: DNS. Windows smart multi-homed name resolution issues parallel DNS/LLMNR/NetBT queries across ALL networks; even the "turn it off" policy still says "DNS queries will be issued across all networks first." So DNS packets keep leaving Ethernet regardless of metric; metric only decides which answer is preferred.

Third: existing TCP connections never migrate. Fourth: IPv4 and IPv6 metrics are independent — set both or IPv6 stays on Ethernet.

claims.claim: Windows route selection = longest matching prefix first, then lowest metric among equal-length matches; ties broken by a predefined rule on destination/source IP. Verbatim: "The route that has the longest match ... is chosen. ... If multiple matching entries are found (for example, multiple routes to the same network ID), the router uses the lowest metric to select the best route."

Total route preference = route metric + interface metric. Verbatim: "the actual route metric used to compute the route preference is the summation of the route metric offset specified in the Metric member of the MIB_IPFORWARD_ROW2 structure and the interface metric specified in this member."

Same statement repeated for admins: "the overall metric that is used to determine the interface preference is the sum of the route metric and the interface metric." Interface metric REPLACED binding order in Windows 10 / Server 2016 (INetCfgComponentBindings::MoveBefore/MoveAfter no longer available).

Windows 10+ automatic interface metric table for NON-wireless (Ethernet) interfaces: >=100Gb→5; >=40Gb<100Gb→10; >=10Gb<40Gb→15; >=2Gb<10Gb→20; >=200Mb<2Gb→25; >=80Mb<200Mb→35; >=20Mb<80Mb→45; >=4Mb<20Mb→55; >=500Kb<4Mb→65; <500Kb→75.

Windows 10+ automatic interface metric table for WIRELESS (NdisPhysicalMediumWirelessLan / WirelessWan / Native802_11): >=2Gb→25; >=500Mb<2Gb→30; >=200Mb<500Mb→35; >=150Mb<200Mb→40; >=80Mb<150Mb→45; >=50Mb<80Mb→50; >=20Mb<50Mb→55; >=10Mb<20Mb→60; >=4Mb<10Mb→65; >=2Mb<4Mb→70; >=500Kb<2Mb→75; >=200Kb<500Kb→80; <200Kb→85.

Wireless table verified live: this machine's Wi-Fi links at 1.2 Gbps (Native 802.11) and Windows assigned InterfaceMetric 30, which is exactly the ">=500 Mb and <2 Gb → 30" row. Highest possible automatic metric on Win10+ is 85. So any manual 'lose' value above 85 reliably loses to any automatic value.
claims.source: local: Get-NetAdapter (Wi-Fi 1.2 Gbps, Native 802.11) + Get-NetIPInterface (Wi-Fi InterfaceMetric 30, AutomaticMetric Enabled)

claims.claim: DEFAULT of fMinimizeConnections on Windows 11 is 1 (Minimize simultaneous connections), NOT 0 and NOT 3. Proven empirically: registry value absent (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WcmSvc\GroupPolicy exists with ValueCount=0) yet WcmQueryProperty(NULL,NULL,wcm_global_property_minimize_policy,...) returns WCM_POLICY_VALUE{fValue=1, fIsGroupPolicy=0} on Windows 11 Education 10.0.26200. fIsGroupPolicy=0 proves it is the built-in OS default, not a GP.
claims.source: local P/Invoke of wcmapi.dll!WcmQueryProperty; raw bytes 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00

claims.claim: Widespread web claims that "the default value is 3" are WRONG (3 = 'Prevent Wi-Fi when on Ethernet' is what DISA STIG V-253364 *requires*, not the OS default). MS docs also say only "The policy is on by default for Windows 8, Windows 8.1, and Windows 10", and map old Enabled ≡ 1.

fMinimizeConnections=1 semantics, verbatim from the on-box ADML: "any new automatic internet connection is blocked when the computer has at least one active internet connection to a preferred type of network. Here's the order of preference (from most preferred to least preferred): Ethernet, WLAN, then cellular. Ethernet is always preferred when connected. Users can still manually connect to any network."

fMinimizeConnections=0 semantics, verbatim: "a computer can have simultaneous connections to the internet, to a Windows domain, or to both. Internet traffic can be routed over any connection - including a cellular connection and any metered network."

Setting minimize-connections off stops ALL WCM disconnects, verbatim: "This policy setting depends on other group policy settings. For example, if 'Minimize the number of simultaneous connections to the Internet or a Windows Domain' is disabled, Windows will not disconnect from any networks."

Raising Ethernet's metric does NOT protect Wi-Fi from WCM. Verbatim: "When considering which multiple connections to maintain, Windows uses many traits to identify the preferred networks. This approach is used only to determine whether to maintain a connection to a given interface, and not for routing." and "Windows doesn't make connectivity decisions based on the link speed or throughput of a network." Keep-priority order is fixed: 1. Ethernet networks 2. Networks manually connected during the current user session 3. domain-connected networks 4. signal strength 5. preferred network list.

Soft disconnect mechanics (why a busy Wi-Fi survives but an idle one dies): "Windows checks the traffic level on the interface every 30 seconds. If the traffic level is above a certain threshold, no further action is taken... When the traffic drops below the threshold, the interface is disconnected." Also "As soon as Windows decides to soft-disconnect an interface, it informs the TCP stack that the network should no longer be used. The existing TCP sessions continue uninterrupted, but new TCP sessions use this interface only if explicitly bound or if no other interface routes to the desired destination."

Boot/resume race that breaks the widget: "When a PC first starts or resumes from standby, all interfaces simultaneously attempt to connect... If multiple interfaces successfully connect, Windows begins soft-disconnecting interfaces immediately." Combined with value 1 blocking new automatic connections while Ethernet is up, Wi-Fi is frequently simply absent after boot with the cable in.

Real-world confirmation of exactly that symptom on Windows 11, with MS answer 'this is by design': "Normally, Wi-Fi will connect automatically is when the Ethernet cable is unplugged... If the cable is connected, it will prioritize the connection and the wireless connection will be disabled."

Registry contract for the fix: key Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WcmSvc\GroupPolicy, valueName fMinimizeConnections, enum with required="true" and NO <disabledValue>. Therefore GP 'Disabled'/'Not Configured' DELETES the value and the OS falls back to its default of 1 — you must explicitly write DWORD 0.

Sibling WCM policy value names in the same key: fBlockNonDomain, fBlockRoaming, fDisablePowerManagement, fSoftDisconnectConnections (Win10 RS3+). fSoftDisconnectConnections default = enabled/not-configured = soft disconnect; DISABLING it makes disconnects immediate (worse for us) — do not touch it.

Strong host model is the Windows Vista+ default, so source-address selection follows the chosen route, not the reverse: "The TCP/IP stack on Windows Vista and later supports the strong host model for both IPv4 and IPv6 and is configured to use the strong host mode by default (the WeakHostReceive and WeakHostSend members are set to FALSE). With the strong host mode, a unicast packet can be sent out a specific interface that does not have the lowest metric for a route by binding the socket to the source address of the specific interface." Verified live: WeakHostSend=Disabled, WeakHostReceive=Disabled on every interface.

DNS leaks out Ethernet regardless of metric. Verbatim from the on-box ADML: smart multi-homed name resolution "improves performance by issuing parallel DNS, link local multicast name resolution (LLMNR) and NetBIOS over TCP/IP (NetBT) queries across all networks. In the event that multiple positive responses are received, the network binding order is used to determine which response to accept." And even when you ENABLE the 'turn off' policy: "DNS queries will be issued across all networks first." Default = not configured = optimized/parallel.
claims.source: C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions\DnsClient.admx + en-US\DnsClient.adml, DNS_SmartMultiHomedNameResolution (valueName DisableSmartNameResolution, key Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient)

claims.claim: Which interface's DNS servers are tried FIRST is driven by interface metric on Win10+ (metric replaced binding order). Classic sequence: query first DNS server on the preferred adapter, wait 1 s; then first server on all adapters for 2 s; then all servers on all adapters at 2/4/8 s.
claims.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/network-subsystem/net-sub-interface-metric ; https://fixyacloud.wordpress.com/2020/01/27/how-does-windows-decide-which-dns-server-to-use-when-resolving-names/ ; https://directaccess.richardhicks.com/2023/09/25/always-on-vpn-and-interface-metrics/ ("Windows will also use the network interface with the lowest metric value as the preferred interface for sending DNS queries by default.")

claims.claim: IPv4 and IPv6 interface metrics are SEPARATE rows (Family = AF_INET vs AF_INET6). Verified live: Get-NetIPInterface -AddressFamily IPv6 returns a completely different set of rows/metrics from IPv4. Steering only IPv4 leaves IPv6 traffic on Ethernet.

SetIpInterfaceEntry requires elevation: "can only be called by a user logged on as a member of the Administrators group... otherwise ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED"; and for IPv4 "an application must not try to modify the SitePrefixLength member... For IPv4, the SitePrefixLength member must be set to 0." Must set Family + (InterfaceLuid or InterfaceIndex); LUID is preferred because "InterfaceIndex... may change when a network adapter is disabled and then enabled... and should not be considered persistent."

windows crate 0.62.2 exposes everything needed. windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::IpHelper::{SetIpInterfaceEntry, GetIpInterfaceEntry, InitializeIpInterfaceEntry, GetIpInterfaceTable, MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW} behind feature Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper (depends on Win32_NetworkManagement). windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::WindowsConnectionManager::{WcmQueryProperty, WcmSetProperty, WcmFreeMemory, WCM_POLICY_VALUE, wcm_global_property_minimize_policy} behind feature Win32_NetworkManagement_WindowsConnectionManager. Also needed: Win32_Networking_WinSock (AF_INET/AF_INET6/ADDRESS_FAMILY), Win32_Foundation, Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis (NET_LUID_LH). Rust sig: pub unsafe fn SetIpInterfaceEntry(row: *mut MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW) -> WIN32_ERROR.

Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceMetric implicitly clears automatic metric: "If this parameter value is set, then the AutomaticMetric parameter is automatically disabled." And on persistence: "If you do not specify this parameter [-PolicyStore], the default entries are created in both the ActiveStore and the PersistentStore." So the PowerShell/netsh path persists across reboots by default.

Programmatic (NSI/IP-Helper) metric changes appear to be ACTIVE-store only. Evidence: 'vEthernet (Default Switch)' shows active InterfaceMetric 5000 with AutomaticMetric=Disabled, yet `netsh interface ipv4 show interface "vEthernet (Default Switch)" store=persistent` reports "Metric : Default" / "Use Automatic Metric : default", and `Get-NetIPInterface -PolicyStore PersistentStore` shows a blank metric for every interface on this machine. Hyper-V re-applies it each boot.
claims.source: local: netsh interface ipv4 show interface ... store=persistent|active ; Get-NetIPInterface -PolicyStore PersistentStore vs ActiveStore

claims.claim: netsh store semantics: 'active' entries are removed at next boot; 'persistent' (the netsh default) survives reboot.

VPN interaction 1 — force-tunnel VPNs win by metric, so our change does not break them: "VPN V4 and V6 default routes (for example 0.0.0.0/0) are added to the routing table with a lower metric than ones for other interfaces." Verified live: ProtonVPN 0.0.0.0/0 sits at RouteMetric 0 with interface metric 0 and beats Wi-Fi's 0+30.

VPN interaction 2 — the VPN's pinned server host-route does NOT follow a metric flip. Verified live: a /32 host route to the ProtonVPN server (203.0.113.10/32 via 192.168.1.1) is bound to ifIndex 14 (Wi-Fi). Flipping metrics does not move it; the tunnel's outer packets stay on whichever NIC was active at connect time, and the tunnel breaks if that NIC later goes away.

VPN interaction 3 — third parties rewrite interface metrics behind your back. Always On VPN / RAS is reported to change the Ethernet interface metric (e.g. 25 -> 4250) while connected and restore it on disconnect, which would silently clobber a LinkSwitch 'parked' value and silently undo the steering.

Metered flag does not steer routes. It changes Windows Update / Delivery Optimization / Store / OneDrive / app behaviour (NetworkInformation cost APIs), not the routing table. The only routing-adjacent statement is inside fMinimizeConnections=0 text ("Internet traffic can be routed over any connection - including ... any metered network"), i.e. metered avoidance is a WCM policy effect, not a metric effect. WCM cost is queried via wcm_intf_property_connection_cost / WCM_CONNECTION_COST_DATA.

This user's likely topology makes the design work cleanly AND removes the usual 'LAN traffic splits' concern: Wi-Fi is 192.168.1.51/24 gw 192.168.1.1, and the (currently unplugged) Ethernet already carries DNS server 192.168.1.1 and connection suffix 'lan' — i.e. both NICs land on the SAME subnet behind the same router. Both interfaces then have an on-link 192.168.1.0/24 route, so the metric decides LAN traffic too and everything moves together (no split brain). On a DIFFERENT-subnet setup, longest-prefix match keeps LAN traffic on Ethernet regardless of metric — which is usually desirable but is a behaviour difference worth surfacing.

WCM_POLICY_VALUE returned by WcmQueryProperty is 8 bytes { BOOL fValue; BOOL fIsGroupPolicy; } and carries the enum in fValue for the 1809+ enumeration semantics (observed 01 00 00 00 | 00 00 00 00). MS docs describe the 1809+ value as "an enumeration available only through Group Policy", so prefer the registry write over WcmSetProperty for changing it.

Rust: read the EFFECTIVE WcmSvc minimize policy (works with no registry value present) — use this to drive a health banner in the widget
THE MANDATORY FIX — run inside --install-tasks (already elevated). Writes 0; does NOT delete.
code.snippet:
$key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WcmSvc\GroupPolicy'
New-Item -Path $key -Force | Out-Null
New-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name 'fMinimizeConnections' -PropertyType DWord -Value 0 -Force | Out-Null
# 0 = "Allow simultaneous connections". OS default when absent is 1 (proved via WcmQueryProperty).
# Do NOT 'delete to disable' — the ADMX enum has no <disabledValue>, so deleting restores default 1.
# Uninstall path: back up the prior state (present/absent + value) and restore it verbatim.
# Effect is picked up by WcmSvc; a reboot (or at minimum a Wi-Fi reconnect) is the reliable path.

code.purpose: Reference implementation of the metric flip in PowerShell (persists to BOTH stores — use this semantics as the target behaviour to match)
code.snippet:
# Park Ethernet (lose), hand Wi-Fi back to Windows (win)
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv4 -InterfaceMetric 9000
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv6 -InterfaceMetric 9000
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Wi-Fi'    -AddressFamily IPv4 -AutomaticMetric Enabled
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Wi-Fi'    -AddressFamily IPv6 -AutomaticMetric Enabled

# Restore Ethernet
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv4 -AutomaticMetric Enabled
Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv6 -AutomaticMetric Enabled

# netsh equivalent (store=persistent is netsh's default):
#   netsh interface ipv4 set interface "Ethernet" metric=9000 store=persistent
#   netsh interface ipv4 set interface "Ethernet" metric=automatic store=persistent

code.purpose: One-shot verification script the implementer should run before/after a flip (proves it worked, and catches the leaks)
code.snippet:
Get-NetIPInterface | Sort AddressFamily,InterfaceMetric |
  ft AddressFamily,ifIndex,InterfaceAlias,InterfaceMetric,AutomaticMetric,ConnectionState -Auto
Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' |
  ft ifIndex,InterfaceAlias,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceMetric -Auto     # total = Route+Interface
Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '::/0' |
  ft ifIndex,InterfaceAlias,NextHop,RouteMetric,InterfaceMetric -Auto     # IPv6 must flip too!
Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress 1.1.1.1 | ft InterfaceAlias,IPAddress,NextHop -Auto  # actual egress+source
Get-NetConnectionProfile | ft Name,InterfaceAlias,IPv4Connectivity -Auto
netsh wlan show interfaces | Select-String 'State|SSID'   # is Wi-Fi even still up?

code.purpose: Rust: classify NICs as Ethernet vs Wi-Fi without string-matching adapter names

gotchas: SHOWSTOPPER: fMinimizeConnections defaults to 1 on Windows 11 (empirically proven on 10.0.26200 with the value absent). LinkSwitch is broken out of the box without the HKLM write — not because routing fails, but because Wi-Fi will not auto-connect while Ethernet is up, so after every boot/resume with the cable in there is no Wi-Fi link to switch to. Ship the fMinimizeConnections=0 write in --install-tasks, and treat it as a first-class, reversible install action the user consents to (it is a machine-wide policy change; say so in the README and the installer output).

Metric changes give Wi-Fi ZERO protection from WCM. MS is explicit that the keep/drop decision uses a fixed media preference (Ethernet > WLAN > cellular) and 'not for routing', and never link speed. Do not assume 'we made Ethernet lose, so Windows will keep Wi-Fi'. It will not.

IPv6 IS A SEPARATE INTERFACE ROW. If you only steer AF_INET, IPv6-capable sites (most large CDNs) still egress Ethernet and the user reports 'it didn't work'. Set AF_INET and AF_INET6 on both NICs, every time. Windows prefers IPv6 over IPv4 by prefix policy (::/0 precedence 40 vs ::ffff:0:0/96 precedence 35 — verified locally).

DNS still leaves Ethernet. Smart multi-homed name resolution issues parallel DNS/LLMNR/NetBT across ALL networks; even the 'turn off smart multi-homed name resolution' policy still emits DNS 'across all networks first'. Metric only decides which adapter is queried first and whose answer wins. Do NOT advertise LinkSwitch as 'zero traffic on Ethernet' — say 'your connections egress Wi-Fi; DNS lookups are still emitted on both'. If a user wants it airtight, the only clean lever is blanking the parked NIC's DNS servers, which is invasive and must be opt-in + restored on flip-back.

Existing connections never migrate. Flipping mid-download does not move the transfer — TCP keeps its 4-tuple and its bound interface. The old path keeps working (Ethernet is still up) so nothing visibly breaks, but the user sees 'my download is still on Ethernet'. This is the opposite of the usual complaint and needs a one-line explanation in the UI: 'applies to new connections; existing transfers finish on their current link.' Long-lived apps (Teams/Discord/Steam/RDP/SSH) will sit on the old link for hours.

SetIpInterfaceEntry appears to write the ACTIVE store only. Evidence on this box: vEthernet (Default Switch) has an active metric of 5000 with AutomaticMetric=Disabled, yet the persistent store reports 'Metric: Default' for it and Get-NetIPInterface -PolicyStore PersistentStore shows a blank metric for every interface. Set-NetIPInterface (no -PolicyStore) writes BOTH stores. Consequence: if you go the IP-Helper route, register an additional Task Scheduler trigger (ONSTART + optionally on network-change / EventID from Microsoft-Windows-NetworkProfile) that re-applies the saved LinkSwitch state, or the parked metric silently evaporates on reboot and on cable replug.

InterfaceIndex is explicitly documented as non-persistent ('may change when a network adapter is disabled and then enabled'). Persist NET_LUID (or the adapter GUID) in config, never ifIndex. Resolve with ConvertInterfaceAliasToLuid / ConvertInterfaceGuidToLuid at apply time.

VPN clients clobber you in two directions. (a) They pin a /32 host route to the VPN server on whichever NIC was live at connect time — verified here: 203.0.113.10/32 via 192.168.1.1 on ifIndex 14 (Wi-Fi). A metric flip does NOT move that route, so the tunnel's outer packets keep using the old NIC. (b) RAS/Always On VPN is reported to rewrite the physical interface metric (25 -> 4250) while connected and restore it on disconnect, silently undoing LinkSwitch. Detect an active VPN (a 0.0.0.0/0 or 0.0.0.0/1+128.0.0.0/1 route on an IF_TYPE_PPP/TUNNEL interface) and either warn or refuse to flip while it is up.

Do NOT 'disable' the GP to fix it. The WCM_MinimizeConnections ADMX element is an enum with required="true" and NO <disabledValue>, so Disabled/Not Configured deletes the value and you land back on the OS default of 1. You must write DWORD 0. Store the pre-existing state (absent vs present-with-value N) and restore it exactly in --uninstall-tasks.

Value 3 ('Prevent Wi-Fi when on Ethernet') is a real deployment: it is what DISA STIG V-253364 mandates for Windows 11. On a STIG'd/managed machine, Windows will refuse even a MANUAL Wi-Fi connection while Ethernet is present, and your HKLM write will be reverted at the next gpupdate by the domain GPO. Detect fIsGroupPolicy==1 from WcmQueryProperty and, in that case, tell the user LinkSwitch cannot work on this machine rather than silently failing.

Safe values: the highest metric Windows ever assigns automatically on Win10+ is 85 (wireless table) / 75 (other). Use 9000 as the 'lose' value — it clears 85 by a mile, clears the RAS 4250 behaviour, sits above Hyper-V's 5000, and stays under 9999 so the classic 'Interface metric' field in the adapter GUI still displays and accepts it. For the 'win' side, do NOT hardcode 5 — set AutomaticMetric back to Enabled and let Windows compute it (this machine: Wi-Fi 1.2 Gbps -> 30). Hardcoding a winner fights the OS on every link-rate change and leaves stale state if LinkSwitch is uninstalled.

Note that route metric is the OTHER half of the sum. DHCP-installed default routes here have RouteMetric 0, so interface metric alone decides — but a user with a manually-added persistent route (route -p add, RouteMetric 256) or a third-party tool can defeat you. Read Get-NetRoute/GetIpForwardTable2 and show the TOTAL, not the interface metric, in the widget.

'Windows responds to Ethernet connections but doesn't automatically manage Ethernet connections' — so there is no WCM-side risk of Windows dropping the Ethernet link itself. The asymmetry is entirely on the Wi-Fi side.

Same-subnet home routers (this user's case: Wi-Fi 192.168.1.51/24, Ethernet DNS 192.168.1.1, suffix 'lan') mean LAN traffic moves WITH the flip because both NICs carry an equal-length 192.168.1.0/24 route. On different-subnet setups (dock + corporate LAN), longest-prefix match keeps LAN traffic pinned to Ethernet no matter what the metric is. Both are correct; the widget should not promise one behaviour.

Soft disconnect is traffic-gated: WCM samples every 30 s and only drops when traffic is below threshold. This produces a maddening intermittent bug class if you skip the fMinimizeConnections fix — Wi-Fi survives while the user is browsing, then vanishes when they walk away, and the widget looks broken only sometimes. Do not let a passing manual test convince you the policy fix is unnecessary.
open_questions: Does writing fMinimizeConnections=0 take effect without a reboot? I could not test — this session is not elevated. WcmSvc is running and GP changes are usually consumed on notification, but every community write-up says 'restart your PC'. The implementer should: write the value, re-run WcmQueryProperty (expect fValue=0, fIsGroupPolicy=1), then confirm behaviourally by plugging Ethernet in and seeing whether Wi-Fi auto-connects. If it requires a restart, --install-tasks must say so plainly rather than leaving the user with a widget that appears to do nothing.

Is SetIpInterfaceEntry active-store-only or does it write through to the persistent store? My evidence is circumstantial (Hyper-V's 5000 is active-only, and the persistent store is empty machine-wide). Definitive test: elevate, call SetIpInterfaceEntry with a metric, then check `Get-NetIPInterface -PolicyStore PersistentStore` and `netsh ... store=persistent`. If it is active-only, either switch to the netsh/CIM path or add the ONSTART re-apply task. This changes the task-registration design, so settle it early.

Exact behaviour of fMinimizeConnections=1 on an ALREADY-connected Wi-Fi when Ethernet arrives on current Windows 11 builds: the 1809+ ADML text only describes BLOCKING new automatic connections, while the WCM concept article still documents soft-disconnect of non-preferred networks. Both are in current first-party docs. Empirically these produce different user reports. I could not test because this machine's Ethernet is unplugged (LinkSpeed 0 bps, 169.254.x APIPA). Worth a 10-minute cable test on the user's own machine before and after the policy write.

Does the widget need to CONNECT Wi-Fi, not just steer to it? If Wi-Fi is down at flip time (very likely pre-fix, still possible post-fix if the profile was 'forgotten' or AutoSwitch is off), the metric change alone yields no internet. Recommend the elevated worker also call WlanConnect (wlanapi) or shell `netsh wlan connect name="<profile>"` and wait for connectivity before/while applying metrics — plus a preflight that refuses to flip to a link that is not connected. This machine's profile shows 'Connection mode: Connect automatically' but 'AutoSwitch: Do not switch to other networks'.

Whether to offer an opt-in 'strict' mode that also blanks the parked NIC's DNS servers (Set-DnsClientServerAddress -ResetServerAddresses) to close the documented parallel-DNS leak. It is the only mechanism that actually stops DNS egress on Ethernet, but it is invasive, must be restored on flip-back, and will strand the user if the app crashes mid-flip. Needs a product decision.

Ranking of alternatives if metrics prove insufficient (my recommendation, best first): (1) interface metric via SetIpInterfaceEntry/Set-NetIPInterface — the documented, supported, fully reversible mechanism, and it is sufficient for ROUTING; keep it. (2) fMinimizeConnections=0 — not an alternative but a mandatory complement. (3) Per-route metric via SetIpForwardEntry2 on the specific 0.0.0.0/0 row — finer-grained and avoids touching the whole interface, but DHCP re-plumbs default routes on every lease renewal/link event and will overwrite you; more fragile, not less. (4) MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW.DisableDefaultRoutes = TRUE on Ethernet — a genuinely interesting stronger hammer (documented for VPN split-tunnel suppression): it removes Ethernet's default route entirely rather than de-preferring it, which also kills the DNS-over-Ethernet path for off-link servers while leaving the link up and LAN reachable. Worth prototyping as an optional 'strict' mode, but it is a blunt instrument and I found no first-party guidance on using it outside VPN clients. (5) Binding order — DEAD; Microsoft removed it in Windows 10/Server 2016 and replaced it with interface metric. Do not implement. (6) Set-NetIPInterface -Forwarding — irrelevant; that controls packet forwarding between interfaces, not egress selection. Do not implement. (7) SkipAsSource — near-useless here: it removes an address from source-address selection and DNS registration, but with the strong host model the source already follows the route, and it does not apply cleanly to a DHCP-assigned primary address. Skip.

refuted.claim: Rust snippet: `row.UseAutomaticMetric = 0;` / `= 1;` with the comment "BOOLEAN maps to u8".
refuted.why_wrong: Proven by compiling the dive's snippet verbatim against windows 0.62.2 (rustc 1.96.1, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): error[E0308] mismatched types, `expected bool, found integer`, twice. windows-rs 0.6x maps Win32 BOOLEAN to Rust `bool`, not u8. Vendored source confirms: `pub UseAutomaticMetric: bool` (registry src .../windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/NetworkManagement/IpHelper/mod.rs:2979). Every BOOLEAN in MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW is `bool` (AdvertisingEnabled, WeakHostSend, WeakHostReceive, Connected, DisableDefaultRoutes...). The dive's snippet does not compile as shipped.
refuted.correction: row.UseAutomaticMetric = false; row.Metric = m;  /  row.UseAutomaticMetric = true;  (and set row.Metric = 0 in the automatic branch so a stale value is not written back).

refuted.claim: NIC classification snippet: "MIB_IF_ROW2.PhysicalMediumType (NDIS_PHYSICAL_MEDIUM): NdisPhysicalMedium802_3 = 1 (Ethernet); NdisPhysicalMediumNative802_11 = 9 (Wi-Fi)".
refuted.why_wrong: NdisPhysicalMedium802_3 is 14, not 1. Value 1 is NdisPhysicalMediumWirelessLan — i.e. the dive's constant would classify a wireless-LAN adapter as Ethernet. Verified in windows 0.62.2 source (Ndis/mod.rs:2645 `NdisPhysicalMedium802_3 = NDIS_PHYSICAL_MEDIUM(14i32)`; :2664 `NdisPhysicalMediumWirelessLan = NDIS_PHYSICAL_MEDIUM(1i32)`; :2654 Native802_11 = 9 — only that one was right). This is exactly the media the dive's own automatic-metric claim lists as *wireless*, so the bug is self-contradictory.
refuted.correction: Ethernet: PhysicalMediumType == NdisPhysicalMedium802_3 (14) && Type == IF_TYPE_ETHERNET_CSMACD (6). Wi-Fi: PhysicalMediumType in {NdisPhysicalMediumNative802_11 (9), NdisPhysicalMediumWirelessLan (1), NdisPhysicalMediumWirelessWan (8)} || Type == IF_TYPE_IEEE80211 (71). Import the named constants from windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::Ndis instead of hardcoding numbers. IF_TYPE_* live in ...::IpHelper and are plain `u32` (IpHelper/mod.rs:1581, 1613).

refuted.claim: "Also filter out virtual junk: MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags.HardwareInterface == 1 and NOT .FilterInterface".
refuted.why_wrong: Those named fields do not exist in windows-rs. The C bitfield is collapsed to an opaque byte: `pub struct MIB_IF_ROW2_0 { pub _bitfield: u8 }` (IpHelper/mod.rs:2743-2745), and MIB_IF_ROW2.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags is of that type (:2707). `row.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags.HardwareInterface` is a compile error.
refuted.correction: Do bit math on `_bitfield` (MSVC allocates the netioapi.h bitfield from the LSB): HardwareInterface 0x01, FilterInterface 0x02, ConnectorPresent 0x04, NotAuthenticated 0x08, NotMediaConnected 0x10, Paused 0x20, LowPower 0x40, EndPointInterface 0x80. e.g. `let f = r.InterfaceAndOperStatusFlags._bitfield; let usable = (f & 0x01) != 0 && (f & 0x02) == 0;` — this compiles (verified) against 0.62.2.

refuted.claim: "SHOWSTOPPER ... Mandatory fix: elevated write of HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WcmSvc\\GroupPolicy!fMinimizeConnections = 0. LinkSwitch is broken out of the box without the HKLM write."
refuted.why_wrong: The empirical part is right (I independently reproduced it: my own compiled Rust calling WcmQueryProperty(NULL, NULL, wcm_global_property_minimize_policy) returns (fValue=1, fIsGroupPolicy=0) on this Win11 26200 box, with the GroupPolicy key present and ValueCount=0). The *conclusion* is overstated. The same MS article the dive quotes lists what Windows KEEPS under the enabled/1 policy: "Any Ethernet network / **Any networks manually connected during the current user session** / The most preferred connection to the internet / ...". And the value-1 text blocks only "any new **automatic** internet connection" — "Users can still manually connect to any network" (confirmed verbatim in the on-box C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions\en-US\WCM.adml). So at the OS default there is a fully supported, non-invasive path: connect Wi-Fi manually; it is then on the keep list and is not a soft-disconnect candidate. Only value 3 blocks a manual WLAN connect while Ethernet is up. A machine-wide security-policy write is therefore a convenience, not a precondition — and it is not free: DISA STIG WN11-CC-000055 / V-253364 requires fMinimizeConnections = 3 and explicitly flags value 0 as a finding, so shipping the write by default silently breaks compliance on any managed box.
refuted.correction: Reorder the design: (1) the elevated worker calls WlanConnect (windows::Win32::NetworkManagement::WiFi) or shells `netsh wlan connect name="<profile>"` and waits for connectivity before applying metrics — the dive buried this in open_questions; it is the primary mechanism. (2) Offer fMinimizeConnections=0 as an OPT-IN checkbox ("keep Wi-Fi connected while Ethernet is plugged in"), backing up prior state (absent vs value N) and restoring verbatim on uninstall. (3) Refuse/warn when WcmQueryProperty reports fIsGroupPolicy=1 or fValue=3.

refuted.claim: "IPv6 IS A SEPARATE INTERFACE ROW ... Set AF_INET and AF_INET6 on both NICs, every time" — implemented as `GetIpInterfaceEntry(&mut row).ok()?`.
refuted.why_wrong: On the user's own machine the AF_INET6 row does not exist for any physical NIC, so this aborts the entire flip. Measured with my own compiled probe: Wi-Fi/Ethernet/ProtonVPN AF_INET all return OK, AF_INET6 all return WIN32_ERROR(1168) = ERROR_NOT_FOUND. Cause: `Get-NetAdapterBinding -ComponentID ms_tcpip6` shows Enabled=False on Wi-Fi, Ethernet, ProtonVPN, Bluetooth and both VMware adapters (only vEthernet (Default Switch) has IPv6 bound). The dive's "Verified live: Get-NetIPInterface -AddressFamily IPv6 returns a completely different set of rows" is technically true but reads as though both NICs had v6 rows — they have none; the IPv6 list here is just Loopback + vEthernet. Same trap on the write side: SetIpInterfaceEntry documents ERROR_NOT_FOUND for "the network interface ... does not match the IP address family specified in the Family member."
refuted.correction: Treat a missing family as success-with-no-op, never as failure: `if e == ERROR_NOT_FOUND || e == ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND { return Ok(Applied::FamilyAbsent) }`. Report per-family status in the widget ("IPv4 steered; IPv6 not bound on this adapter") so a v6-disabled box does not look broken. Verified to compile against 0.62.2.

refuted.claim: "VPN interaction 3 — RAS/Always On VPN is reported to change the Ethernet interface metric (e.g. 25 -> 4250) while connected and restore it on disconnect, which would silently clobber a LinkSwitch 'parked' value." (source: directaccess.richardhicks.com, admitted "via search summary")
refuted.why_wrong: I opened the cited article. It does not say this. It states only that "Windows automatically assigns metric values to network interfaces (including VPN interfaces) based on ... connection speed, link state, and interface type" and then recommends *manual* administrator-set metrics (PowerShell / rasphone.pbk / DPC). There is no claim of automatic rewriting of a PHYSICAL adapter's metric, and no 25->4250 figure. Worse, first-party doc points the other way: MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW/SetIpInterfaceEntry Remarks frame RAS metric-bumping as a Windows XP / Server 2003 weak-host-model behaviour and say that on Vista+ "The route metric modification by RAS has no effect."
refuted.correction: Drop the 4250 story. The *real*, locally verified VPN hazards are the two I could reproduce: ProtonVPN's 0.0.0.0/0 at RouteMetric 0 on an interface with Metric 0 (total 0, beats Wi-Fi's 0+30), and a pinned host route 203.0.113.10/32 via 192.168.1.1 on ifIndex 14 (Wi-Fi) RouteMetric 30 that a metric flip does not move. Still detect an active tunnel and warn; just don't claim it rewrites your parked metric.

refuted.claim: "Which interface's DNS servers are tried FIRST is driven by interface metric on Win10+ (metric replaced binding order)." cited to learn.microsoft.com/.../net-sub-interface-metric
refuted.why_wrong: I fetched that page in full. It is 221 words and says nothing about DNS. Its only ordering statement is "The order in which adapters appear in a list is determined by the IPv4 or IPv6 interface metric" — about GetAdaptersAddresses enumeration order, not resolver behaviour. The only support for the DNS claim in the dive is two third-party blogs. Note the on-box DnsClient.adml still says the *binding order* decides which positive response is accepted — text that predates the Win10 removal of binding order, so first-party guidance here is stale and self-contradictory.
refuted.correction: Mark DNS-server preference ordering as UNVERIFIED / no first-party source. What IS first-party and does hold: parallel queries go out on all networks regardless of metric (DnsClient.adml, verified verbatim on-box), so present DNS as "still emitted on both links" and do not promise the Ethernet resolver stops being consulted.

refuted.claim: Apply plan: "--apply ethernet => set_iface_metric(eth, *, None); set_iface_metric(wifi, *, None)" and gotcha "For the 'win' side, do NOT hardcode 5 — set AutomaticMetric back to Enabled and let Windows compute it."
refuted.why_wrong: Handing both NICs back to automatic does not guarantee Ethernet wins — read the two tables the dive itself quoted correctly. Non-wireless 80-200 Mb -> 35, 20-80 Mb -> 45. Wireless 500 Mb-2 Gb -> 30, >=2 Gb -> 25. So on a 100 Mbps Ethernet port (old dock, powerline, cheap switch) automatic gives Ethernet 35 against this machine's Wi-Fi 30, and the 'Ethernet' button silently routes over Wi-Fi. MS also adds a multiplier the dive missed: "For half-duplex interfaces, such as wireless, the effective speed is half of the advertised speed" — so a 2.4 Gbps Wi-Fi 7 link is bucketed at 1.2 Gbps -> 30, not 25.
refuted.correction: Make the design symmetric: whichever leg must lose gets the parked value; the winner goes back to automatic. `--apply ethernet` = park Wi-Fi at 9000 (v4+v6), Ethernet -> automatic. `--apply wifi` = park Ethernet at 9000, Wi-Fi -> automatic. `--apply auto` = both automatic. Then verify the outcome (GetIpForwardTable2 / Find-NetRoute) rather than assuming it.

refuted.claim: "Set-NetIPInterface ... on persistence: 'If you do not specify this parameter [-PolicyStore], the default entries are created in both the ActiveStore and the PersistentStore.' So the PowerShell/netsh path persists across reboots by default."
refuted.why_wrong: The quote is real but cherry-picked from a paragraph that contradicts itself. The full -PolicyStore block reads: "The default value is ActiveStore. Specify ActiveStore only." AND THEN "If you do not specify this parameter, the default entries are created in both the ActiveStore and the PersistentStore." MS documents two mutually exclusive defaults on the same page, so this cannot be cited as settled. Local evidence is ambiguous too: Get-NetIPInterface -PolicyStore PersistentStore lists every interface with a BLANK metric, and there is not a single `InterfaceMetric` value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\* on this box.
refuted.correction: Do not design around "PowerShell persists, IP-Helper doesn't". Settle it with one elevated experiment (set a metric, reboot or check PersistentStore + the Tcpip registry) and, until then, ship the ONSTART re-apply task unconditionally — it is correct under either answer and costs nothing. netsh's own default store=persistent IS confirmed by first-party docs and is the safer belt-and-braces path.

added_gotchas: ERROR CODES YOU WILL ACTUALLY SEE (measured, not guessed): GetIpInterfaceEntry/SetIpInterfaceEntry return WIN32_ERROR(1168) ERROR_NOT_FOUND when the family isn't bound on that NIC; WIN32_ERROR(2) ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND when the LUID/index doesn't exist at all; ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5) unelevated. Branch on all three separately — 1168 is normal, 5 means your Task Scheduler plumbing failed, 2 means your saved LUID is stale.

SitePrefixLength = 0 IS LOAD-BEARING, AND THE ROUND-TRIP IS NOT A NO-OP. My probe shows GetIpInterfaceEntry returns SitePrefixLength = 64 for IPv4 on both Wi-Fi and Ethernet on this machine. SetIpInterfaceEntry docs: "for IPv4, an application must not try to modify the SitePrefixLength member. For IPv4, the SitePrefixLength member must be set to 0." So a naive read-modify-write WILL fail until you zero it. Corollary the dive missed: SetIpInterfaceEntry writes back the whole row, so the read-modify-write also re-asserts NlMtu, DadTransmits, RouterDiscoveryBehavior, LinkLocalAddressBehavior, ZoneIndices etc. as explicit values. MS warns about exactly this ("Caution must be used with this approach because the only way to determine all of the fields being changed would be to compare..."). Highest-risk field is NlMtu: netsh persistent shows "Link MTU: Default" but the active row reads 1500 — writing 1500 back may pin an MTU that was previously derived from the link. Diff the row before/after in testing.

AN UNPLUGGED ETHERNET REPORTS METRIC 5 WITH AutomaticMetric=Enabled. Measured here: Ethernet ifIndex 4, LinkSpeed 0 bps, Status Disconnected, Connected=false, UseAutomaticMetric=true, Metric=5 — which is the ">= 100 Gb" row of a table it obviously doesn't belong to. Never render "who would win" in the widget from the published speed table or from a link-down interface's current metric; read the actual routing table (GetIpForwardTable2 / Get-NetRoute) and show RouteMetric + InterfaceMetric, which is what the stack actually compares.

WCM's keep-list has an escape hatch the dive treated as a dead end. Under fMinimizeConnections=1 Windows maintains "networks manually connected during the current user session." That is the supported way to hold Wi-Fi up next to a live Ethernet with no registry change. UNVERIFIED and worth a 10-minute cable test: whether a programmatic WlanConnect counts as "manual" for WCM, or only a click in the network flyout. Settle this before deciding whether the policy write ships on by default.

MS contradicts the dive's quoted priority list one paragraph later: the list ends "4. Signal strength of the currently connected Wi-Fi network / 5. The PC's preferred network list", but the same article then states flatly "Windows 10 doesn't use the Wi-Fi signal strength." Don't build any UI text or logic on item 4.

WRITING fMinimizeConnections=0 IS A COMPLIANCE REGRESSION, NOT JUST AN INVASIVE TWEAK. DISA STIG Windows 11 WN11-CC-000055 / V-253364 requires the value 3, and its check text makes value 0 an explicit finding. On any STIG'd or Intune-baselined machine your write is both non-compliant and transient (reverted at the next policy refresh). Say this in the README and in the installer output, and detect fIsGroupPolicy=1 before offering it.

UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION UNDERNEATH THE 'detect value 3 and refuse' plan: WCM_POLICY_VALUE.fValue is typed BOOL (windows_core::BOOL, i32) — verified in the 0.62.2 source — and the 1809+ semantics stuffed a 0..3 enum into it. I observed 1, which is indistinguishable from a boolean TRUE. Nobody has shown that a GP-set 3 comes back through WcmQueryProperty as 3 rather than being normalised to 1. Read HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WcmSvc\GroupPolicy!fMinimizeConnections directly (read-only, no elevation needed) as the authoritative source for the *enum*, and use WcmQueryProperty only for the effective-default case where the value is absent.

LEAK + ERROR HANDLING BUG in the dive's wcm_minimize_policy(): it returns None on `data.is_null() || size < 8` without calling WcmFreeMemory, and it treats a non-zero rc as 'no data' without surfacing which error. WcmQueryProperty really does return a bare `u32` in 0.62.2 (verified: `pub unsafe fn WcmQueryProperty<P1>(pinterface: Option<*const GUID>, strprofilename: P1, property: WCM_PROPERTY, preserved: Option<*const c_void>, pdwdatasize: *mut u32, ppdata: *mut *mut u8) -> u32`), so `rc != 0` compiles — but free the buffer on every path where ppdata came back non-null, and prefer casting to the real struct: `let v = *(data as *const WCM_POLICY_VALUE);` with `WCM_POLICY_VALUE { fValue: BOOL, fIsGroupPolicy: BOOL }`.

SECURITY HOLE IN THE ELEVATION DESIGN (routing-adjacent, and it will get the project pilloried on release): an unelevated widget triggering a HIGHEST-run-level scheduled task is the classic UAC-bypass shape. If the task's action takes the metric value, the adapter identity, or a config path as arguments supplied by the unelevated caller, any local process can drive an elevated network reconfiguration. Register FIXED verbs only (`--apply ethernet`, `--apply wifi`, `--apply auto`, no parameters), have the elevated worker read the config from a location only Administrators can write (ProgramData with an explicit DACL, not %APPDATA%), and validate the parked value server-side against a hardcoded allowlist.

CARGO FEATURE NUANCE: `Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper` alone is not sufficient for the types you need. MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW is `#[cfg(all(feature = "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis", feature = "Win32_Networking_WinSock"))]` and MIB_IF_ROW2 is `#[cfg(feature = "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis")]`. The dive's feature list happens to include them, but if anyone trims it the failure is a confusing 'cannot find type' rather than a missing-feature hint. Add `Win32_NetworkManagement_WiFi` when you implement the WlanConnect preflight. All six listed features exist verbatim in 0.62.2 (confirmed by `cargo add`, which enumerated them and reported 662 deactivated features).

VERSION SANITY: `windows` is still 0.62.2 (published 2025-10-06) as of today per the crates.io API, and that is what `cargo add windows@0.62` resolves to under rustc 1.96.1. docs.rs deep links for this crate 404 (per-item pages aren't built at that scale) — read the vendored source under ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/windows-0.62.2/src/Windows/Win32/... or microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs instead of trusting a docs.rs URL that was never opened.
verification.verdict: Trustworthy on the WINDOWS BEHAVIOUR, not trustworthy on the RUST. Build on it, but rewrite the code. The routing model (longest prefix, then route metric + interface metric), the two Win10+ automatic-metric tables, the strong-host-model consequence, the elevation and SitePrefixLength requirements, the netsh store semantics, and — most importantly — the headline WCM finding all survived adversarial checking; I independently reproduced fValue=1/fIsGroupPolicy=0 with my own compiled WcmQueryProperty call on this Win11 26200 box with the registry value absent, and every "verbatim" ADMX/ADML/learn.microsoft quote I checked was accurate rather than paraphrased. That is unusually good. The Rust is the opposite: the flagship set_iface_metric snippet does not compile (BOOLEAN is `bool`, not u8), the NIC-classification snippet has a wrong NDIS constant that would label Wi-Fi as Ethernet plus two struct fields that don't exist, and the error handling aborts the whole flip on this user's own machine because IPv6 is unbound on every physical NIC here (ERROR_NOT_FOUND 1168). Two citations were oversold: the Always-On-VPN "25 -> 4250" gotcha is not in the article it cites (the dive admits it only read a search summary), and the DNS-ordering claim is cited to a 221-word page that never mentions DNS. Finally, downgrade the framing: fMinimizeConnections=0 is a strongly-useful opt-in, not a mandatory install action — MS documents manually-connected networks as protected from soft disconnect and manual connects as always permitted at values 0/1/2, so WlanConnect (which the dive filed under open questions) is the primary mechanism and the machine-wide policy write is the convenience layer, one that also makes the box STIG-noncompliant. Net: keep the prose, replace the code, and settle the two experiments the dive correctly flagged (does SetIpInterfaceEntry persist; does the policy write need a reboot) before locking the task-registration design.

dive.topic: Empirical proof-of-concept on this Windows 11 machine: windows-rs 0.62.2 IP Helper metric/route APIs (read-only) + eframe 0.36.1 borderless transparent always-on-top widget
dive.summary:
All risky parts were built and run for real on this box (rustc 1.96.1, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc). Nothing was mutated: only Get* APIs were called, no scheduled tasks, no registry writes.

**windows crate = 0.62.2.** The whole point of the task: `Win32_NetworkManagement_IpHelper` alone does NOT expose the needed APIs. In 0.62.2, GetAdaptersAddresses, GetIpInterfaceEntry, SetIpInterfaceEntry, GetIpInterfaceTable, GetBestRoute2 and MIB_IPINTERFACE_ROW are each gated behind `#[cfg(all(feature = "Win32_NetworkManagement_Ndis", feature = "Win32_Networking_WinSock"))]`. The exact working feature list is those three features and nothing else. `Win32_Foundation` is transitively enabled (verified by importing WIN32_ERROR/NO_ERROR without listing it), though listing it explicitly is harmless. `FreeMibTable` is the one API gated only by IpHelper.

netpoc compiled warning-free and ran; every native value matches PowerShell ground truth exactly (10 interfaces, identical metrics).

**Design-critical discovery: GetBestRoute2 toward 8.8.8.8 returns InterfaceIndex 43 = ProtonVPN, not Wi-Fi (14).** A WireGuard tunnel holds a 0.0.0.0/0 route at RouteMetric 0 and InterfaceMetric 0 with UseAutomaticMetric=false. So the widget's "which link is winning?" indicator must NOT naively use GetBestRoute2 or it will show the VPN forever, and metric steering between Ethernet/Wi-Fi will appear to do nothing while a VPN is up.

Second trap: this machine has three IfType-71 adapters — real Wi-Fi (14) plus two "Microsoft Wi-Fi Direct Virtual Adapter" (16, 17). Selecting "the Wi-Fi adapter" by IfType alone picks the wrong one. Similarly IfType 6 matches VMware VMnet1/8 and a Hyper-V vEthernet.

**eframe = 0.36.1**, and it has a breaking trait change most tutorials predate: `App::update(&mut self, ctx: &Context, ...)` no longer exists; the required method is `fn ui(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, frame: &mut Frame)`, and `CentralPanel::show` now takes `&mut Ui`, not `&Context`. `clear_color` survives. The borderless/transparent/always-on-top viewport not only compiled but actually launched a live window (verified, then killed). glow renderer: 6.7 MB / 190 deps vs default wgpu 14.3 MB / 422 deps — use glow.
